Mikayla Matthews is leaving The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives amid turmoil in MomTok.
The influencer and Hulu star shared the news in a social media post as the cast was recently seen in Italy filming Season 6 of the reality series.
“I made my decision over a week ago, after hearing some news, that I will not be continuing the show at this moment,” Matthews posted on Instagram. “I’ve said from the beginning of this that I’m not comfortable being a part of something that continues to platform behavior I don’t agree especially given my own experience growing up in a home with multiple forms of abuse.”
She continued, “There’s no amount of money worth going against my morals or changing the stance I’ve had since I first saw and heard the things that made me feel this strongly. And for me personally, continuing to directly profit from this behavior feels wrong and unethical. It feels like a disservice to the children, everyone’s healing and the millions of people watching.”
Watch on Deadline
Matthews is seemingly referring to her co-star Taylor Frankie Paul, whose personal life has been at the center of drama on Secret Lives of Mormon Wives since the first season. Production for Season 5 of the series was paused after domestic violence allegations from Paul’s ex, Dakota Mortensen, with whom she shares a child. Legal actions, a custody battle, and an old resurfaced video showing Paul physically assaulting Mortensen were released ahead of the release of The Bachelorette, which prompted ABC to cancel its premiere.
On the most recent season of SLOMW, Matthews and Paul clashed over the latter not wanting any criticism of her life. Although Matthews and Paul mended things on camera, things off-camera didn’t seem to be good.
Matthews points out that the children ultimately suffer from continuing to expose their troubling lives on camera. Hulu will seemingly continue to work with Paul, which Matthews doesn’t think is good for her mental health or for the rest of the cast and their children.
“This show has been a huge part of my life and has helped me provide for my family,” Matthews continued. “I’m so grateful for the experience, and will continue sharing my story, my health and advocating for myself and others this shouldn’t be ‘relatable’ or entertainment in anyway. Supporting an ADULT doesn’t mean constantly making excuses for toxic behavior while giving unconditional sympathy and grace with zero accountability or change. I was in that enabling cycle for years, and I’m not going to be a part of that again! love you all.”

What is MSI mode on Windows PCs and does it speed up your GPU?
It's a setting you probably won't want to mess around with.
MSI (Message Signaled Interrupts) mode is a Windows feature designed as a way for hardware devices like your graphics card (or GPU, if you're a purist) to grab the attention of and communicate with your CPU. Introduced in the PCIe 2.2 specification and then baked into Windows Vista, it's a specialized setting that modders and tweakers all too often talk (recklessly) about as if it's some hidden performance unlock.
While, yes, it's true that switching MSI on can genuinely trim latency on older cards that use the line-based interrupt method, you shouldn't really be touching it. MSI won't raise your average frame rate if you've got an older card, and most modern graphics card drivers, like those for the RTX 5090, enable MSI by default in most cases. If you force it on hardware where the manufacturer chose not to, you could render that device unresponsive until you undo the change.
What is MSI used for?
Your CPU is your PC's "brain," responsible for executing instructions by decoding their binary code and issuing commands. When a component like your graphics card needs to stop what it's doing, it sends an interrupt request, or IRQ, to the CPU via a dedicated hardware line. But since there's only so many of these physical lines, lots of devices can end up cramming onto one, causing latency when the shared line can't tell the CPU which device fired a signal.
Instead of relying on hardware lines, a device that uses MSI raises an IRQ by writing a small value to a specific memory address instead. Every interrupt arrives already labeled with its sender as a result, meaning that it never collides with another device's traffic. The introduction of PCI 3.0 in 2010 brought MSI-X, an extended version that supports more individual messages. Windows now uses this as the default whenever a device offers both, whether you're still on Windows 10 or have made the upgrade to Windows 11.
In terms of what your graphics card stands to gain, the most noticeable change will be consistency over speed. With MSI, interrupts are serviced with less waiting around, which can settle frame pacing and reduce input latency on a system that was otherwise suffering from congested lines. Your card won't render any faster; MSI requests mean your graphics card gets a higher response priority from your CPU. That's it. If it's outright speed you're after, our guide on how to buy a GPU will serve you better.
Controversial take: Manufacturers know best
MSI is controlled by the registry value MSISupported, and it's the manufacturer's GPU driver that writes it during installation. Most current-gen AMD graphics card drivers come with MSI enabled, as do the drivers for many recent NVIDIA models. If you've got a graphics card where MSI is disabled by default, however, that's a decision that the manufacturer has made as a compatibility judgment call. It's unwise to assume it's an oversight and override it; doing so runs the risk of crashes and driver timeouts on hardware with a flawed MSI implementation.
There's a pretty good example of an MSI failure in action available on the Dell support website. It republished Microsoft guidance covering a failure where certain SSDs running Windows 10's default StorAHC.sys driver stopped completing reads and writes with MSI mode enabled, pinning Task Manager at 100 percent disk utilization. The fix in this case was to switch MSI off for the affected controller.

On 26 August 2026, massive flash floods struck parts of Nepal and Tibet, causing widespread destruction (here, here, and here). In this context, a video is being shared on social media (here, here, and here) claiming it shows a mother and her daughter being swept away in the Nepal floods. Let’s verify the truth behind the video in this article.
Claim: The video shows a mother and her daughter being swept away in the 2026 Nepal floods.
Fact: The video does not show a mother and daughter being swept away in the 2026 Nepal floods. It shows two sisters being swept away by floodwaters in the Philippines in September 2025 before they were rescued by residents. Hence, the claim made in the post is Misleading.
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to several media reports published in September 2025 (here, here, and here) featuring the same visuals. According to these reports, the incident occurred on 4 September 2025 in Barangay Balogo, Guihulngan City, Negros Oriental, Philippines, where two sisters were swept away by a strong current while returning home from school. They clung to tree roots and were later rescued by local residents.
To sum up, an old video of sisters trapped in a flash flood in the Philippines is shared as footage from the 2026 Nepal floods.

Six Nigerian nationals linked to an organized criminal network that allegedly swindled American women out of more than $6m through online romance scams were extradited to the United States on Friday.
South African police confirmed they were to be extradited earlier on Friday, while local news in Africa confirmed that the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation, known as the Hawks, facilitated their handover to officials from the US Federal Bureau of Investigation and Secret Service at Cape Town international airport, in collaboration with Interpol South Africa.
The men, who were arrested in the South African city of Cape Town in 2021, face wire fraud and money laundering charges.
They are accused of belonging to a criminal network known as the Black Axe, which Interpol describes as being among criminal groups responsible for a significant share of the world’s cyber-enabled financial fraud, typically through romance, cryptocurrency and investment scams.
According to South African police, the men are alleged to have targeted more than 100 women in the US, defrauding them of more than $6m through online romance or love scams.
Among the alleged victims were pensioners and businesspeople who were reportedly targeted through sophisticated online relationships.
“Through the coordination of Interpol South Africa, the six will today be transported from a correctional facility in Cape Town to Cape Town international airport, where they will be handed over to officials from the FBI and the United States Secret Service, who arrived in South Africa this morning,” said police spokesperson Katlego Mogale.
A recent operation by Interpol targeting west African organized crime groups led to the arrest of 58 people and the identification of 263 suspects linked to various criminal networks involved in similar crimes, the multinational police body said last month.
The operation aimed to disrupt money laundering, identify high-value targets, seize assets, and support arrests and prosecution.
In South Africa, authorities raided seven locations in the city of Johannesburg linked to a syndicate that ran romance and investment scams targeting retirees in English-speaking countries.
In that operation in South Africa, police arrested 39 people, seized $2.67m and froze more than 250 bank accounts, Interpol said.

New Delhi: India and the South American trade bloc Mercosur have begun negotiations to expand their existing trade agreement, the commerce ministry said on Monday, as New Delhi seeks to diversify export markets and deepen trade ties amid global economic turmoil.
The agreement, operational since June 2009, currently provides India with duty concessions on 450 tariff lines, or product categories, while Mercosur offers concessions on 452. Bilateral trade between India and the bloc stood at $21 billion in 2025.
Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal and Uruguay's minister of foreign affairs Mario Lubetkin announced the start of the negotiations, according to the the commerce ministry statement.
Both sides are "in the process of finalising the terms of reference, which will define the scope and structure of the future expanded agreement," it added.
Mercosur comprises Brazil, Argentina, Bolivia, Uruguay, and Paraguay. The move comes as India seeks to broaden its export base, while its strong growth prospects amid global turmoil have prompted countries and trading blocs to deepen economic engagement with New Delhi.
India has signed several trade agreements in recent years with economies including the European Union, the UK, the United Arab Emirates and Australia. The country has remained the world’s fastest-growing major economy since 2021-22, and the International Monetary Fund expects it to retain that status for at least the next two years. Its economy expanded at a higher-than-expected pace of 7.8% in the June quarter of fiscal year 2027 (Q1FY27) despite external headwinds.
Separately, India and Mercosur signed a protocol on Monday to facilitate paperless trade and modernise customs procedures.
“The move is expected to facilitate the transition towards digital and paperless trade documentation, reduce transaction costs and processing time associated with the issuance and verification of Certificates of Origin, and improve the efficiency of preferential trade under the existing India-Mercosur preferential trade agreement (PTA),” the commerce ministry said.
The initiative follows deliberations in the Joint Administrative Committee of the India-Mercosur PTA. At a meeting in November last year, both sides supported updating the agreement to enable the use of digital certificates of origin. The proposal was subsequently adopted by mutual consent at the fifth meeting of the Joint Administrative Committee on 9 April 2026.

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Sunday (September 13, 2026) resorted to satire to target the Mohan Yadav government over the deaths of tribal children in Balaghat district and posted a tongue-in-cheek letter on X about his "resignation" as "Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh".
The letter, addressed to MP Governor Mangubhai Patel and dated August 13, has Mr. Dipke stating that he was resigning as "my conscience does not allow me to continue occupying this chair after the deaths of more than 30 tribal children in Balaghat".
He also thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi for giving him the "opportunity to serve the people of MP", an opportunity he said he had "clearly failed" to make the most of.
The satirical letter took aim at the government's handling of the Balaghat deaths, particularly the compensation announced for the victims’ families.
Mr. Dipke also questioned if compensation of "₹24 lakh" was adequate had these been the children of ministers or MLAs.
As per Balaghat additional collector DP Burman, kin of 24 deceased kids have been given ₹4 lakh each, while the process is on to give aid to the others.
In the letter, Mr. Dipke said the deaths of innocent children "demand accountability at the highest level".
The post then widens its sweep, taking potshots at the government's claims on tap-water supply, education and tribal welfare.
Mr. Dipke pointed out that some tribal families in Balaghat still depend on river water and alleged schools in several villages are in a condition worse than animal shelters.
He also cited government data on tribal households without electricity, crimes against Scheduled Tribes and malnutrition among children to underline what he called the failures of successive BJP governments in the State.
Concluding his mock resignation letter, Mr. Dipke said he had "failed the tribals of not just Balaghat but the entire State" and, after the loss of so many innocent children, did not believe he had "the moral right to continue in this office".
The post came a day after Mr. Dipke's visit to disease-affected villages in Balaghat, where his interaction with families was disrupted by a confrontation with a group of social media influencers.
Earlier this week, the Jabalpur Bench of the Madhya Pradesh High Court sought a response from the State government over the deaths of more than 30 children allegedly due to infectious diseases in Balaghat district.
A Division Bench of Acting Chief Justice Vivek Rusia and Justice Pradeep Mittal issued notices to the State Health Department, Women and Child Development Department, Balaghat Collector and others while hearing a public interest litigation.
The PIL alleged inadequate treatment for children and claimed that around 400 children were being treated at a hospital with a capacity of 50 beds.
It also alleged that yellow-coloured water was coming from handpumps in the affected areas and that children and women had not received nutritious food on time for several months.

On September 5, Saurav Das, the co-convener of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), shared a photo on X that attributed a quote to BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia, under the label of ‘NBT’, which presumably referred to the news outlet, NavBharat Times.
It was claimed that Bhatia had said, “The youth named Swatantra Bhardwaj is a ‘Dimaagi Naxal’, he is filled with casteist venom, and he has nothing to do with the BJP government.”
The post was later deleted by Das, but the archived version can be accessed here.
Several other X users, like Nimo Yadav (@DrNimoYadav), Vaibhav Shukla (@vaibhaw_g), and Gen-Z of India (@GenZ_of_India_) amplified the viral quote. Archives: 1, 2, 3
Bhardwaj, a Hindutva hardliner, recently created an uproar after a clip from a podcast went viral. In it, he boasted about assaulting Sanjay Kumar, father of CJP protester Nishu Azad, during the Jantar Mantar protest, and asserted that he faced no action because of his political connections, naming Kapil Mishra and Chirag Paswan. He now faces criminal charges under Sections 115(2), 126(2) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, along with provisions of the POCSO Act and SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, with an attempt-to-murder charge also invoked in the case. On September 7, he was sent to 14-day judicial remand.
Fact Check
To verify the authenticity of the viral quote attributed to Gaurav Bhatia, we ran relevant keyword searches to see if any verified news outlet reported on it, but could find none.
However, we found this X post, published by Navbharat Times on September 5, which clarifies that “misleading messages are being spread” through these “fake posts.”
पिछले कुछ दिनों से सोशल मीडिया पर NBT के नाम से कई पोस्ट वायरल हो रही हैं और उन फ़र्ज़ी पोस्ट के जरिये भ्रामक संदेश फैलाए जा रहे हैं। NBT की किसी भी खबर की सत्यता जांचने के लिए केवल NBT के आधिकारिक सोशल मीडिया हैंडल पर ही भरोसा करें। #FactCheck #NBT #FakeNews pic.twitter.com/rA9pC6iHS3
— NBT Hindi News (@NavbharatTimes) September 5, 2026
Thereafter, we found that Gaurav Bhatia had also categorically debunked the viral quote attributed to him by Saurav Das, in an X post. He gave the CJP leader an ultimatum of 24 hours to apologise for spreading the viral misquote, warning that he would file an FIR against him otherwise.
It took only 83 minutes for the post to be deleted. Unqualified apology still remains. Tomorrow will be a day of FIR if no unqualified apology is tendered. Can’t spread propaganda and then just delete and run. https://t.co/oTXLR6ZwKe
— Gaurav Bhatia गौरव भाटिया 🇮🇳 (@gauravbhatiabjp) September 5, 2026
Das himself shared a post stating that the quote-graphic was AI-generated.
To sum up, the viral quote attributed to BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia about Swatantra Bhardwaj being a ‘Dimaagi Naxal’ is entirely fabricated. Bhatia had made no such statement on the Hindutva propagandist who is now in jail facing multiple criminal charges including under POCSO Act.

In August and September 2026, a claim recirculated online that U.S. President Donald Trump told People magazine that Republicans are "the dumbest group of voters in the country."
"If I were to run, I'd run as a Republican," the purported 1998 Trump quote begins. "They're the dumbest group of voters in the country. They believe anything on Fox News. I could lie and they'd still eat it up. I bet my numbers would be terrific."
The claim previously spread on social media platforms like Reddit, Threads and X in the summer of 2024. We also found the quote shared on Imgur in 2023 and on TikTok in 2020.
We found no evidence that Trump ever said the quote in question.
We previously wrote about the quote in 2015 and 2020. People magazine previously confirmed to FactCheck.org that it had no record of having published any such interview or exchange with Trump:
People looked into this exhaustively when it first surfaced back in Oct. [2015]. We combed through every Trump story in our archive. We couldn't find anything remotely like this quote -- and no interview at all in 1998.
Our research in People's archives, which are no longer available on its website, found that in 1998 the magazine covered Trump mostly for his relationships with his first and second wives, Ivana Trump and Marla Maples. While there is evidence Trump was interested in politics during the late '90s, nothing we found proved he ever said anything about "dumb Republicans" to any reputable publication.
For further reading, we examined a rumor that Trump criticized the National September 11 Memorial & Museum in New York City because he wasn't allowed to speak at its 25th-anniversary remembrance of the 9/11 attacks.

With the public release of iOS 27 and tvOS 27, Apple Home is getting an injection of Apple Intelligence — but you’ll have to pay more for it.
Apple Home’s new security camera features cost up to $60 a month
Apple Intelligence upgrades to HomeKit Secure Video come with a steep cost.
Apple Intelligence for Home brings AI-powered video summaries to HomeKit Secure Video, so you can get short text descriptions of who and what compatible security cameras saw, along with the clip. It also adds a new video search feature and the ability to stitch footage from multiple cameras into one clip, making it easier to keep an eye on what’s happening around your home without scrolling through footage.
But to get these features, you’ll need to pay $9.99 a month for the 2TB iCloud Plus plan (or $39.95 a month for an Apple One Premier subscription) — and that’s just for one camera. According to an Apple support page, to add Apple Intelligence to a second camera, you’ll have to pay $29.99 a month for the 6TB plan. For up to five cameras, it’s a whopping $59.99 a month for the 12TB plan. No word on whether you can add more than five cameras. (Recordings from HomeKit-connected cameras don’t count toward your storage quota.)
That’s way too expensive. While the improved video features are useful — I’ve been testing them in beta and have been impressed — they’re not good enough to justify that big a price jump.
HomeKit Secure Video has always been behind a paywall, but it started at a very reasonable $1 a month. That’s for the 50GB iCloud Plus plan, which includes recorded footage from one camera, plus smart alerts and facial recognition. For more cameras, you bump up to 2TB / $9.99 a month (up to five), and 6TB / $29.99 a month or higher for unlimited cameras. But the cost for the Apple Intelligence features is a huge increase.
I currently pay $40 a month for Apple One Premier, which includes 2TB of iCloud storage and gets me HomeKit Secure Video support for five cameras. With the new pricing tier, I keep those benefits and now get Apple Intelligence on one camera. But to get it on all five cameras, I’d need to pay an additional $60 a month. That’s $720 a year, for a total of $1,200.
Amazon’s Ring and Google Nest charge around $20 a month for subscription tiers that include similar AI-powered features for their cameras, and both companies offer more features than Apple currently does. An iCloud Plus plan does include storage for photos, files, and device backups, and higher plans may get you higher limits for Siri AI and other Apple Intelligence features, but Apple hasn’t released any details about that.
The good news is that none of this changes what you get with HomeKit Secure Video today, and the new software releases have added under-the-hood upgrades that improve speed and reliability, plus the service now supports 4K video resolution. But while Apple Intelligence feels like a significant improvement for Apple Home, at these prices, the value just isn’t there.

President Donald Trump has spent years making false claims about election fraud, including his refusal to accept that he lost the 2020 presidential election to Joe Biden. Since that election, Republicans who denied or questioned the results have taken positions on local election boards, worked inside election offices, trained poll observers, and sought to influence state election laws.
The 2020 election deniers running in swing states
Gubernatorial candidates in multiple swing states have questioned the 2020 election results. How worried should you be?
Now, as we head into the 2026 midterm elections, candidates who have denied or questioned the results of the 2020 election are running for governor and other powerful positions in key swing states. If elected, some could play important roles in overseeing future elections.
Today, Explained co-host Sean Rameswaram spoke with Andrew Kaczynski, senior reporter at CNN who has been reporting on election-denying candidates and what their victories could mean for future elections.
Below is an excerpt of the conversation, edited for length and clarity. There’s much more in the full podcast, so listen to Today, Explained wherever you get podcasts, including Apple Podcasts, Pandora, and Spotify.
Which swing states are having elections featuring candidates who have denied the 2020 election results?
The interesting thing is that we talked about in this article that we did on the five most key swing states is governor’s races. We’re talking Arizona, Pennsylvania, Michigan, and Wisconsin and Georgia. These are all states that Trump won in 2016, Biden in 2020, then Trump in 2024. And what we had talked about was how in each of these states, there are candidates running for governor who in four of the cases just outright denied the results of the 2020 election.
How are these candidates in these five races faring? Does it look good for any of them?
With the caveat that we’ve seen some pretty big polling misses already in two of these states, most of these candidates are behind in the polls, but there’s always the caveat that these are states that Trump won in 2024 and 2016. So they’re going to be, they’re true battlegrounds. So anything could really happen in them.
And how much is their dispute or lie about the 2020 election coming up in their races?
Not a ton, but what we did see was when we did this story, pointing out that at least in four of the key states, these are candidates that outright denied the election. When we reached out to three of them, they immediately gave us statements saying they would accept whoever won in their states in 2028. They would certify the winner. They said that Biden did win in 2020.
So we’ve seen election denial is kind of a liability, it would seem for these candidates. Just to give you the example of Michigan, John James has been down by five or six in some of the polls. He was somebody who originally got elected in a swing seat in 2022 as a member of Congress after he had two failed Senate runs. And he was like, “Yeah, of course Biden won in 2020.” And then when he ran this time, he actually went the other direction when he maybe was trying to get Trump’s endorsement. There’s a rally where he said that Trump won Michigan three times, which obviously did not happen.
So you have a situation where it is probably a liability. A couple of these candidates are running from him, but at least two of them, Andy Biggs and John James, didn’t say that Biden won in 2020, didn’t say they’d certify the winner, and didn’t really give us a comment at all on that. But three of them said they would certify the winner.
Do you see this as part of a broader effort on the part of this administration, or the Republican Party more broadly, to sort of legitimize the Big Lie into our institutions, into even election administration, which there’s been lots of reporting about? Or is it just a coincidence? Are there so many election deniers now that, inevitably, some of them are going to be running for office in key battleground states?
I think it’s more the latter. It was just so thoroughly embedded in the Republican Party in 2020 and Trump had such a stranglehold over the party. But in 2022, many of those big election denier proponents that he backed, they did lose. So I do think it’s more of a liability for these candidates, but. It’s also why Trump supports a lot of them.
We’ve got a lot of candidates who deny the results of the 2020 election running for office in 2026. We’ve got people who deny the results of the 2020 election administering our elections in various key battleground states. We’ve got the Supreme Court fighting with lower courts about what maps they can use. We’ve got the president trying to redraw the rules around mail-in voting.
What do you think this all amounts to for President Trump? Is this about the midterms? Is this about 2028? Is this just a pastime of his?
It’s a pastime. It all runs through the fact that he thinks, or is lying, that he won in 2020, and this is all just a part of it. It’s all part of the same delusions about mail-in voting or fraud, or this or that. There’s an example of Andy Biggs, who’s running for governor in Arizona. He was a huge, huge stop the steal proponent and he was like, The governor could have de-certified the results if they wanted to, and that couldn’t obviously happen. And that’s what Trump likes. John James, who said it at a rally with Trump: He won Michigan three times.
Trump just likes that. Trump likes the candidates who lie and say that he won in 2020. It’s just like a pastime of his trying to find this fraud that doesn’t — like, obviously it exists. Obviously people do commit voter fraud at very low levels, but never has it been shown that it ever is on a large scale or enough to change the election.
Do we have any sense of whether the frustration people have with Donald Trump, and his real policies, can overcome all of the shenanigans we’re seeing around our elections so far this midterm season?
Yes. I think if we have really close races in the House, Senate, governor, that’s where I think some of this stuff could come into play with people denying the election, saying they won, trying to throw out ballots or this or that.
Election fights, that’s where things could get into a shit show. But I don’t think we’ll be talking about this if [Democrats] win by pretty good sized margins. And obviously Trump can say whatever he says, but the results will be the results — it’s like that.

Thousands demand end to violence in Mexican cartel hotspot
- Published
Thousands of people have taken to the streets of Culiacán to demand an end to the violence that has wracked the city in northern Mexico.
The state of Sinaloa has seen the number of murders and disappearances skyrocket since two factions of the Sinaloa cartel started a bloody war two years ago.
Residents dressed in white held up posters of missing loved ones and signs reading "We don't want fear, we want peace" at the protest on Sunday.
More than three million people live in Sinaloa and many say that the war between the two rival factions - known as Los Chapitos and La Mayiza - has blighted their lives.
The march was scheduled to coincide with the second anniversary since the start of the conflict - which broke out after the arrest of wanted drug lord Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada in the US.
His followers, La Mayiza, allege he was betrayed by the son of the infamous founder of the Sinaloa cartel, Joaquín "El Chapo" Guzmán, and have turned on members of his faction, Los Chapitos.
The two factions regularly carry out ambushes, drive-by shootings and erect roadblocks by hijacking trucks, which they set alight.
Residents of Culiacán have been caught up in this internecine war.
Not only has the number of murders and disappearances shot up in the state but also those of extortions and robberies, official figures suggest.
Sunday's protest was organised by relatives of victims, local businesses, civil society groups and the Catholic Church.
Businessman Sergio Esquer told AFP news agency that more than 5,000 businesses had closed since the start of the feud.
"That's the tragedy Sinaloa is experiencing," Esquer, who is a leader in the centre-left opposition party Movimiento Ciudadano, said.
The event started with a Mass in which the bishop of Culiacán called on members of the warring groups to put an end to their violence.
"Stop, look at what's happening, look at the affected families, look at the young people and at our city. No amount of power, of money, territory or ambition is worth more than a human life," he said.
Among those who attended the protest were relatives of a one-year-old boy who died after being hit by a bullet in the head during a shootout in the city last week.
As well as the wave of violence, Sinaloa state has also been hit by political upheaval in recent months.
In April, US prosecutors accused the state's governor, Rubén Rocha, and nine other current and former officials of conspiring with Los Chapitos to smuggle drugs into the US.
Rocha, who has denied any wrongdoing, stepped down temporarily while Mexican prosecutors opened an investigation of their own into the allegations.
Three weeks ago, he returned to his post, but just days later requested another leave of absence after President Claudia Sheinbaum wrote on social media, without directly naming him, that "power without principles becomes arrogance".

I Filled a Tent With Smoke to Find the Best Air Purifiers
Featured in this article
No matter where you live, the best air purifier for you is one that is tailored to your specific clean-air need. I lived in Los Angeles and San Francisco for almost a decade, including during some of the most severe wildfires the region has seen in recent years. Beneath an eerily yellow sky with smoky, stagnant air, I donned an N95 mask as a bartender—long before the pandemic made masking the norm. Needless to say, I'm no stranger to bad air and can appreciate the value of a good air purifier.
Now I live in New York City, where the threat of wildfires ravaging large swaths of land is less imminent, but contaminants from cars and buses, cigarette smoke, and building and industrial emissions are ever present. Not to mention the volatile East Coast weather that's known to host newsworthy pollen spikes, and more recently, wildfire smoke drifting down from Canada. Plus, I live in a tiny apartment with a gas stove and no hood vent (yikes!), and I also have two very furry cats and a roommate who is allergic to them. So, while my focus may be less on outside air quality, I wage a daily battle fighting pet dander and microscopic allergens in my home.
We tested each purifier throughout our real homes and in a sealed tent with smoke pellets. We measured visual smoke clearance, time to return to healthy air-quality readings, noise levels, room coverage, app performance, and filter design. The budget Coway Airmega Mighty2 ($270) is the best choice for most people, and the IQAir Atem X ($1,400) is our premium pick if you prioritize design and long-term repairability over price. I'm continuously testing new models to stay up-to-date with the best air purifier for every budget, room size, and pollutant.

How Do I Test Air Purifiers?
I have started a uniform testing method for every air purifier I test, measuring each unit’s efficacy by using a sealed tent and smoke pellets to see how quickly each air purifier clears the pellet smoke and returns the air to healthy quality when on auto mode. I measure first visually, using a timer to measure how long it takes to clear the smoke by eye. Then I measure how long it takes for the air quality to return to healthy, using both my air quality monitor and the connected app or display on the air purifier machine. I then add up the time and am able to compare models with concrete data. I also use a decibel meter on my phone to calculate noise levels during sleep and auto modes, as well as at its highest setting, since air purifiers can be egregiously loud on their most powerful setting.
So for each model, I take into account how long it took on auto-adjustment settings for the air to visually clear the smoke bomb, and then use the app or machine to calculate how long it takes to measure back at healthy levels. I also use each for nearly a month, moving around my house to test in different locations: when cooking on my unventilated gas stove, under my living room window that draws in a lot of building and exhaust fumes, and outside my cat's litter box, measuring if and when the air purifier auto-engages and how long it takes to get back to clean air quality.

How to Shop for an Air Purifier
How does a busy shopper find the right size purifier for a room they want to clean? The CDC recommends that one should aim for five air exchanges per hour, in a metric known as the ACH. When looking at an air purifier, look at the cubic feet per minute in airflow at the lowest setting. When measuring the cubic footage of your room, you need the area of the room times the height. Imagine a one-foot cube of styrofoam: How many cubes could you fit into a room?
Anyone shopping for an air purifier also needs to look for two acronyms and terms. First, look for CARB certification, which means that that unit passed the rigorous standards of the California Air Resources Board. Next, check the filter type (broken down below). Also, don’t forget to unwrap your filter! There’s a special kind of horror that comes with realizing you’ve been running your air purifier with a plastic-wrapped HEPA filter.
HEPA Filters: This is a high-efficiency particulate air filter that can remove at least 99.97 percent of dust, mold, pollen, bacteria, and airborne particles as small as 0.3 microns. It's a great option for those who suffer from allergies or respiratory issues, since it can help to clear out airborne particles that can trigger symptoms—like sneezing, sore throat, difficulty breathing, coughing, and more. It's worth noting, however, that HEPA filters don't remove volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from the air the way activated carbon filters do. But these are typically paired with carbon filters.
Activated Carbon: Activated carbon filters (also known as activated charcoal) are highly effective because they are very porous and have a large surface area—allowing the filters to absorb gas pollutants, odors, and VOCs. They’re best for removing fumes, smoke, and chemicals from the air. But these filters have to be replaced more often depending on the environment. For example, if there’s a wildfire in your area and the air purifier is working more intensely than usual, it’s important to replace a saturated filter to avoid toxic gases from being released back into the air.
Washable Air Filters: A few of the options I've listed in this guide come with washable prefilters in addition to a HEPA and/or activated carbon filter—which is what you'll typically find. These are the most cost-effective since you don't have to buy new ones each time you need to replace a filter. Simply remove it, scrub it with soap and water, and let it dry.
UV-C Sanitizer Filters: Ultraviolet filters use UV light to kill viruses, parasites, mold spores, and bacteria. They can't remove airborne particles, VOCs, or gas pollutants, so they're only fully effective when combined with a HEPA filter. According to the EPA, UV lights without proper lamp coatings have the potential to emit ozone. I recommend checking this list from the Association of Home Appliance Manufacturers for models that have been shown to emit little to no ozone. —Lisa Wood Shapiro
How to Check Your Air Quality
Many large states and cities are required to report the local outdoor air quality index (AQI), which was established by the EPA and measures the concentrations of major air pollutants, like ground ozone and carbon monoxide, that are regulated by the Clean Air Act. We like AirCare (iOS, Android), but your state or county may have even more localized apps.
To check if your indoor air quality stacks up, consumer monitors like the Airthings View Plus ($330) also measure carbon dioxide, temperature, and humidity, in addition to pollutants and particulate matter (PM) of various size, including the notably health-compromising PM 2.5. Need more information? Check out our complete guide to checking your air quality. —Lisa Wood Shapiro
How Does WIRED Select Air Purifiers to Review?
We look at popular models from all brands—both new and long established—and at all price points, taking into consideration features, size, effectiveness, and consumer popularity. Companies themselves often provide samples with the understanding that editorial coverage is not guaranteed. WIRED does earn affiliate revenue from purchases, but this does not factor into our editorial decisions.
What Do I Do With Air Purifiers After Testing?
A handful of top picks are kept around for longer-term testing, evaluation against new picks, and for use in testing auxiliary products like food dehydrators and the Plantaform indoor smart garden, but all others are donated locally, including to organizations like NYC public schools.

Five baby orangutans have been found in a forest in India, prompting authorities to investigate if they were trafficked into the country from south-east Asia.
The orangutans, native only to the islands of Borneo and Sumatra and known for their shaggy red fur, were found in Balasore district of Odisha state, thousands of kilometres away from their natural habitat.
Odisha’s environment minister, Ram Singh Khuntia, said wildlife investigators were trying to establish how the rare apes reached India.
“We suspect that an international racket might be involved in this,” Singh said.
International commercial trade in orangutans is prohibited under Cites – a global agreement governing trade in endangered wildlife.
The five babies were found by forest department officials who were patrolling in the Jaleswar range in Balasore district.
Officials believed the orangutans had been in the area for just a few days, and they have now been placed in quarantine at a zoological park in Odisha.
According to the World Wildlife Fund, about 104,000 orangutans remain in Borneo and Sumatra, down from more than 230,000 a century ago.
The Tapanuli orangutan (Pongo tapanuliensis), a third species, is classified as critically endangered, with fewer than 800 believed to survive in the wild.
In November, conservationists found the Tapanuli population had been reduced by 7% after severe flooding in Indonesia.
Between 33 and 54 Tapanuli orangutans were estimated to have been killed in widespread floods and landslides in North Sumatra province.
Previous research has suggested annual losses of 1% of the Tapanuli orangutan population would be sufficient to lead to eventual extinction.
The entire Tapanuli population dwells solely in the West Block of the Batang Toru, a forest threatened by mining, palm oil plantations and a large hydropower project.

The Supreme Court has put the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India’s (FSSAI) two-phase rollout of front-of-pack warning labels (FoPL) under the scanner, warning that the second phase could be “indefinitely postponed” in the absence of a clear timeline. The court also asked the Centre to consider introducing nutritional education in schools to help children understand food labels and make informed dietary choices.
Under the proposed rollout, warnings would initially apply to packaged foods high in two or more nutrients of concern — added fat, added sugar and salt — and would be extended in the second phase to products high in even one of them. The FSSAI had proposed the phased approach to give consumers time to adapt to the new labels and the food industry time to reformulate its products.
“Assessment of consumer acceptability or giving the industry adequate time for reformulation cannot be reason enough for this uncertainty in time. Therefore, a reasonable, scientifically justified and clearly defined timeline or transitionary period which divides the two-phases must be indicated, for the approach of the FSSAI to be a workable one,” a Bench comprising Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran said in an order passed on Thursday (September 10, 2026) night.
It accordingly asked the FSSAI to consider an alternative model, under which products with the highest levels of nutrients of concern would be brought under the warning regime first, followed by those with progressively lower thresholds.
‘Nutritional literacy’ in schools
Acknowledging that children are particularly “vulnerable” to “impulse or uninformed dietary decision-making”, the Bench also asked the Union government to incorporate nutritional literacy into school curricula, including teaching children how to interpret nutritional information and front-of-pack labels.
The top court passed the directions while hearing a PIL filed by non-profit 3S and Our Health Society, represented by advocate Rajiv Shankar Dvivedi, seeking mandatory front-of-pack warnings on packaged foods high in sugar, salt and saturated fats.
‘Scientific basis’
The court also questioned why a warning should initially require a product to be high in at least two nutrients of concern when excess levels of even one could pose health risks. It noted the petitioners’ contention that the two-nutrient requirement lacked scientific basis and would leave many products outside the first phase.
The Bench also took note of concerns raised by stakeholders against placing ultra-processed foods on the same footing as minimally processed packaged foods, given the greater nutritional benefits of the latter. It accordingly asked the regulator to consider whether different thresholds could be formulated based on the degree of processing.
The FSSAI was further asked to clarify which “specified sweetened beverages” would be covered in the first phase and the thresholds that would apply to them.
‘Insufficient information’ on labels
The order also raised questions about the design of the proposed warning labels. The FSSAI has proposed a red hexagon carrying warnings such as “HIGH FAT”, “HIGH SUGAR” and “HIGH SALT”, but the court flagged that there was “insufficient information” on its size and placement.
It also pointed out that a “strictly word-based warning label” presupposes a certain level of comprehension and literacy among consumers, potentially limiting its accessibility across regions, languages and age groups.
“Ideally, an all-inclusive FoPL which effectively caters to the diverse population of this country should incorporate a combination of words along with pictorial representations of the individual nutrients-of-concern. This would ensure that the information provided in the FoPL is truly accessible”, the Bench said.
While acknowledging that the FSSAI had made “significant progress” in implementing its directions on warning labels, the Bench cautioned that reducing salt, sugar and fat in packaged foods could have the “unintended and unfortunate consequence” of prompting manufacturers to increase their use of artificial preservatives, emulsifiers and other additives to preserve taste, texture and shelf life.
It accordingly asked the regulator to “keep this danger in mind” while finalising the threshold limits and considering corresponding regulations governing the addition of such chemicals to packaged foods.
10 days time
The court directed the FSSAI to file an affidavit within 10 days setting out its responses and clarifications on the concerns raised and posted the matter for further hearing on September 28.
The order came a day after Additional Solicitor General Brijender Chahar, appearing for the Centre and the FSSAI, told the court that it was open to making warning labels mandatory for packaged foods high in even one nutrient of concern — sugar, salt or fat — marking a regulatory pivot from the earlier proposal to trigger warnings only when a product exceeded limits for two or more such nutrients.
Earlier, the top court had asked the regulator to take its directions “seriously”, stressing its concern over the impact of food safety standards on public health, particularly that of growing children. “We are concerned with the health of people, more particularly growing children. We have taken it up very seriously... We expect one and all to extend cooperation in a cause which is in national interest,” Justice Pardiwala had said.

DHS did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

తెలంగాణ బీజేపీ నేత, కేంద్ర హోం శాఖ సహాయ మంత్రి బండి సంజయ్ కుమార్ తన కుమార్తెను ఒక క్రైస్తవుడికి ఇచ్చి క్రిస్టియన్ పద్ధతిలో పెళ్లి చేశారంటూ కొన్ని పోస్టులు (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ) సోషల్ మీడియాలో ప్రచారంలో ఉన్నాయి. ఇందులో ఎంత నిజముందో ఇప్పుడు చూద్దాం.
క్లెయిమ్: బీజేపీ నేత బండి సంజయ్ తన కుమార్తెను ఒక క్రైస్తవుడికి ఇచ్చి క్రిస్టియన్ పద్ధతిలో పెళ్లి చేశారు.
ఫాక్ట్: వైరల్ ఫోటోలో ఉన్నది బండి సంజయ్ సోదరుడి కుమార్తె సంజన. బండి సంజయ్కి ఇద్దరు కుమారులు మాత్రమే ఉన్నారు. ఆగస్టు 2026లో సంజనకు దొంతు రజనీక్రాంత్తో హిందూ సాంప్రదాయం ప్రకారం వివాహం జరిగింది. కావున, పోస్టులో చేయబడిన క్లెయిమ్ తప్పు.
ముందుగా బండి సంజయ్ కుటుంబ వివరాలను పరిశీలించగా, ఆయనకు ఇద్దరు కుమారులు మాత్రమే ఉన్నట్లు తేలింది. ఆయనకు కుమార్తె లేదు. 2024 లోక్ సభ ఎన్నికల అఫిడవిట్లో కూడా తనకు ఇద్దరు కుమారులు (సాయి భగీరథ్, సాయి సుముఖ్) ఉన్నట్టు ఉంది.
ఇక వైరల్ ఫోటోలో కనిపిస్తున్న యువతి, బండి సంజయ్ సోదరుడు బండి శ్రావణ్ కుమార్ కుమార్తె సంజన.
మీడియా కథనాల ప్రకారం (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ & ఇక్కడ) , దొంతు హరిప్రసాద్, దొంతు రాణి దంపతుల కుమారుడైన దొంతు రజనీకాంత్తో(రజనీక్రాంత్) సంజన వివాహం ఆగస్టు 2026లో జరిగింది. వీరు క్రైస్తవులు అని ఎక్కడా పేర్కొనలేదు. పైగా, పెళ్లి, రిసెప్షన్కు సంబంధించిన వీడియోలను(ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ & ఇక్కడ) పరిశీలించగా, ఇవి హిందూ పద్ధతిలోనే జరిగినట్లు స్పష్టమవుతోంది.
చివరిగా, బండి సంజయ్ తన కుమార్తెకు క్రిస్టియన్ తో పెళ్లి చేశారంటూ జరుగుతున్న ప్రచారంలో ఎలాంటి వాస్తవం లేదు.

The Birth of the New Legal Right
Forty-four years ago, a conservative legal convention offered disaffected students an identity—and hope.
America’s highest court didn’t take on a deeply partisan, conservative bent overnight. This transformation began decades ago, with a simple purpose: In the early 1980s, three law students were fed up with what they saw as a liberal monoculture at their elite universities. They wanted a place to freely debate conservative ideas and to refine their arguments. So the students—Lee Liberman, Steve Calabresi, and David McIntosh—decided to build one.
In late April 1982, their newly formed group, the Federalist Society, held its first conference, at Yale University. The formal title of the three-day affair was “A Symposium on Federalism: Legal and Political Ramifications,” but the snoozy name belied the energy of the weekend. Young Reaganites packed their sleeping bags and overnighted on the floors of fellow students they’d never met before. During smoke breaks, they chatted up Robert Bork, the famous Yale professor, and Antonin Scalia, then a lesser-known professor from the University of Chicago.
But if the attendees were idealistic about the Reagan era and the emergence of a harder-core strain of conservatism known as the New Right, they also understood that they were still a tiny minority in both the academic and legal worlds. Movements opposed to racism, sexism, and injustice remained the animating forces of campus life. Many students across the country were embracing Marxism and socialism. To make headway, young conservatives needed a voice—and a strategy.
To this end, Bork proved essential. He had recently been nominated by President Ronald Reagan to serve on the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals and spoke with both knowledge and authority. Bork announced to his eager audience that media and academia had become left-wing machines. The Supreme Court was inventing new “rights” with no basis in the Constitution, he said, and the only path forward was to return to the words of the Founding Fathers.
Whether Bork truly believed in the conspiracies he outlined or whether he was merely exaggerating is unclear. But in his remarks at that first Federalist Society conference, Bork effectively mapped out what the right-wing legal movement would do over the course of the next four decades.
“We have a Court,” Bork declared in his speech, “which is creating individual rights which are not to be found in the Constitution by any standard method of interpretation.”
He went on to outline the formation of a nascent conservative approach called originalism. In the originalist view, constitutional rights existed only as the Founding Fathers imagined them, unless officially added via constitutional amendment. By embracing what Bork called a “strict” or “textualist” reading of the Constitution, conservatives could argue that recent social changes never specifically considered by the Founders were not constitutionally protected. The approach could return the country to its true, “conservative” values.
In championing this interpretation of the law, Bork proved to be ahead of his time. He saw benches and courtrooms as the final frontier in the right-wing culture war. Effete liberals either had persuaded judges to ignore the Constitution, he said, or had themselves colonized the bench. Bork railed against the media and academia as corrupting influences: “The institutions to which the court responds are the press and the law-school faculties. Those are the people they talk to; those are the people who are responsible for the reputations of individual judges.”
And those people were liberals. Bork cited a survey from the magazine Public Opinion, which concluded that the people who worked in American media were “heavily left liberal.”
More than 80 percent of the press, he continued, had voted for the Democratic candidate in every presidential election since 1968. The values of the press were “egalitarian and permissive.” And professors were no better: “They want sexual freedoms; they want freedom for abortions; they want the death penalty outlawed.”
Bork believed academic elites were bastardizing the First Amendment and the Fourteenth Amendment to suit their ends, creating “new constitutional values which are nothing more than the imposition of upper-middle-class values on society.” He blamed the “enormous industry in the law schools” and their faculty for these invented “rights.” If the professors had their way, he warned, they would indoctrinate a new class of law students that would promote liberal ideals on benches across the country. This all added up to, Bork stated with thinly veiled disgust, “the gentrification of the Constitution.”
Bork closed his remarks by outlining the constitutional means by which the New Right could overturn federal protection for abortion. Abortion and “acceptable sexual behavior” were matters for the states to decide—not constitutionally protected rights, as Roe v. Wade had recently found. Reproductive freedom, Bork advised, was “a classical case for local control. There is simply no national moral consensus about abortion, and there is not about to be.”
Soon, the Reagan administration would call upon the students that Bork had trained to carry out this strategy of curtailing rights, one case at a time. Four decades later, the Roberts Court would echo Bork’s language when it struck down Roe.
If the Federalist Society had begun as a campus alt-community, it quickly blossomed into something much more important. As Calabresi, one of its co-founders, later recalled, “Our conference was covered by the National Review and suddenly conservatives at fifteen other law schools began calling us and telling us they wanted to attend the conference and they wanted to form chapters, too. That was a process of almost spontaneous generation.” Less than a year after the 1982 Yale conference, 17 law schools across the country had a Federalist Society chapter.
Soon after its inception, the student group was on the White House’s radar. In attendance at that first conference were several members of the Reagan Justice Department, including the future acting solicitor general and the next assistant attorney general at the Office of Legal Counsel. By 1985, all three founding members of the Federalist Society—Liberman, Calabresi, and McIntosh—had positions at DOJ.
Half a century later, every sitting Supreme Court justice appointed by a Republican president is a member of the Federalist Society. During the first Trump presidency, 46 of his 54 nominees to the federal appeals courts were members. His White House counsel, two attorneys general, and deputy attorney general were all members as well.
From that very first conference, the Federalist Society awoke a power lying dormant among marginalized conservatives. It offered them an identity, a larger community, and hope—clarifying the battle at hand and, most essentially, suggesting that they might win it.

Emergency responders have rescued a Chinese man and a Nepali woman in two separate operations as authorities continued to search for thousands of people missing 10 days after massive floods hit Nepal.
The Nepali military said on Saturday a joint team comprising personnel from its army and South Korean disaster experts rescued the man from a 225-metre (740ft) tunnel in the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, and that he was undergoing a health assessment. Pictures showed him being evacuated by helicopter after being carried out of the tunnel.
Rescue efforts have focused on a dozen hydropower projects across Nepal, where about 900 workers are missing, 500 of whom are thought to be trapped in huge tunnels. International rescue teams from India, China, South Korea and the US have been searching through debris and damaged structures at the projects to try to find survivors.
Two Nepali workers were rescued from another tunnel in a hydro-station on the Trishuli River on Friday.
Experts have said the possibility of finding missing people alive in the tunnels is diminishing.
The Nepali woman, 64, was rescued from a damaged house in the devastated town of Nuwakot. Photos published by the Nepali army showed rescuers discovering the woman submerged in mud before she was pulled to safety and airlifted to Kathmandu for treatment. 
 Members of Nepal’s police force cheered as she was pulled from the home, the lower half of which was buried in thick sludge.
Emergency responders have been working to find survivors from the devastating floods in Nepal, which were triggered by a glacial and rock collapse on 26 August. Their work has been complicated by the massive infrastructural damage caused by the floods, with more than 40 bridges having collapsed and rivers swelling unpredictably.
At least 1,375 people have been killed in the floods, with more than 5,000 missing, according to Nepal’s disaster management agency.

One blockbuster listing after another is keeping India’s startup IPO market buzzing. After Shiprocket’s strong debut last month, ESDS extended its post-listing rally for the sixth consecutive trading session on Friday, with the stock now up 306% from its IPO price of ₹429. Now, the spotlight is shifting to furniture rental startup RentoMojo. If its IPO subscription is anything to go by, investors are already lining up for the next big listing. The ₹1,256 Cr issue closed with a whopping 72.88X overall subscription, led by a strong QIB response, while retail investors subscribed 15.59X. The IPO, which opened on September 9 and closed on September 11, attracted bids for 158.7 Cr equity shares against 217.7 Cr shares on offer. The frenzy was not confined to the primary market either. In the grey market, Rentomojo shares were commanding a premium of around 37% on Friday, adding further fuel to the listing buzz. What makes RentoMojo’s subscription numbers striking is the crowded IPO calendar the issue had to contend with. The furniture rental company was competing for investor attention with five other mainboard IPOs that opened on September 9, with some issues attracting significantly more muted demand. If one is to look at the broader trend, a steady flow of money into mutual funds is keeping the sentiment around IPOs buoyant. At the same time, investors are increasingly shifting capital from the secondary market to the primary market, with even FPIs redirecting money towards new listings. "There is also a growing FOMO around companies that can show strong fundamentals. Recent listings such as ESDS Software, which has more than doubled from its IPO price in a week of trading, have given investors another reason to chase the primary market," an analyst said. While RentoMojo is not in the software game, it has the numbers to support some of this enthusiasm which may be trickling into consumer services. Its operating revenue rose 45.5% to ₹387 Cr in FY26, from ₹266 Cr in FY25, while profit after tax jumped nearly 142% to ₹104.3 Cr from ₹43.1 Cr. However, the latter was partly boosted by a ₹36.6 Cr tax credit. Beyond the numbers, is there a trigger behind investors flocking to back the IPO? RentoMojo’s Asset-To-Revenue Flywheel While RentoMojo is being seen as a consumer services business, its real moat lies in the physical infrastructure and the operations systems that power the furniture rentals and the subscription model. For the sake of simplicity, it can be viewed as an asset-utilisation business wrapped in a technology and subscription layer. In this case, RentoMojo buys the assets i.e. furniture and appliances and offers them through rentals to customers who pay a fee each month. When the tenure expires or the customer terminates the service, the company recovers the assets, refurbishes them and puts them back into circulation. By March 31, 2026, RentoMojo had 8.51 Lakh live items, with 83.34% of them being rented out. Management estimates that its furniture and appliances can remain useful for about 10 years. Some of its older assets are showing the benefit of that model. More than 56% of the assets added in 2017 and 60.92% of those added in 2018 were still generating revenue in FY26. Assets added in 2017 had already generated revenue equivalent to 5.12X their original cost. That is where the business can build a flywheel. The more often an asset is rented, refurbished and put back to work, the more revenue RentoMojo can extract from the original investment. The company describes this through three linked engines: ecommerce to acquire customers, subscriptions to generate recurring revenue and manage credit, and recommerce to recover and redeploy assets. RentoMojo says its supply chain infrastructure, operations systems and technology layer ties the three together. This includes tracking assets, forecasting demand and churn, optimising logistics and monitoring refurbishment. Redseer estimates India’s home furniture and appliance rental market grew from about ₹350 Cr in 2021 to ₹1,550 Cr in 2025, and could reach roughly ₹6,030 Cr by 2030. Rentomojo already had an estimated 42-47% share of the organised market in FY25. The Other Side Of The Model The same model that gives RentoMojo an easy route to operating leverage also increases complexities. The company has to not only spend money to acquire customers, but throughout the lifecycle of the customer and even after the customer has ended the relationship. The cost of collections, refurbishing and redeploying the asset has to be recovered through the rental fees and other costs paid by the customer during the lifetime of their relationship. Maximising this and recovering the cost faster will be the key challenge for RentoMojo. One way to do that will be to increase the cost of rentals, but this could adversely affect new customer acquisition. So the journey to maximising the profits will need the right spurs at different levels. In FY26, RentoMojo spent ₹28 Cr on logistics, ₹38 Cr on contractual manpower, ₹19 Cr on refurbishment and ₹21 Cr on performance marketing. These are recurring costs that can rise as the company adds subscribers and expands its asset base. As a listed company, these cost centres will become a key focus for investors examining the company’s trajectory. Depreciation is another important part of the equation. This rose 44% to ₹70 Cr in FY26 as the company invested more heavily in rental assets. At a certain point, assets will have to be written off and the model and category is such that procurement of new assets cannot halt. These are risks that investors have not yet had to consider because the company’s disclosures are only just beginning. The company needs to keep its assets productive for longer, control refurbishment costs and redeploy them quickly when customers return them. This makes the quality of RentoMojo’s profits an important metric to watch. RentoMojo has a growing market, a strong market position and the ability to generate revenue from the same asset multiple times. But investors will also want to see whether that growth can translate into sustainable profits. As of March 31, 2026, RentoMojo had 2.54 Lakh live subscribers across 29 cities and 8.51 Lakh live rental items, according to its RHP. Investors will be watching both numbers closely, particularly the company’s asset utilisation rate, as it expands. Competition adds another layer of potential risk for investors in the long run. Furlenco is said to be eyeing an IPO in the second half of 2027. The RentoMojo rival saw a 20X growth in profits in FY26, which has allowed it to start talking to investors to raise a pre-IPO round as well as a public listing in the next 12-14 months. RentoMojo’s First-Mover Premium RentoMojo is the first established player in its category to go public. This scarcity could work in the favour of the IPO investors and the listing could be at a high premium though nothing is certain. A similar pattern played out with Urban Company’s listing last year. Limited float and the scarcity value attached to a consumer tech IPO could result in high initial gains, but the real test anyway will be whether RentoMojo can sustain earnings after the listing. If the stock lists at a high valuation, the margin for error will be small. Investors are likely to watch the next three to four quarters to see whether profitability holds up as RentoMojo scales. The narrative is familiar in the startup ecosystem: companies can post strong IPO numbers, step up spending on new categories or markets after listing, and see profits come under pressure again. For RentoMojo, the primary objective will be to not be part of this narrative. How to fix Outlook's "Your message can't be displayed right now" error
An annoying error thankfully has a relatively simple fix.
Given how many people use (or are forced to use) Outlook, it's no surprise that errors pop up often. Even the Artemis II crew had to seek tech support for Outlook issues, and it was earlier this year when Microsoft had to issue multiple emergency Outlook patches after it became unusable for many. When you're in the middle of important communication, getting an error that says "Your message can't be displayed right now" is irritating. But the fix is simple.
The method of solving this error depends on whether you're using Outlook in a web browser or the desktop client, but both fixes involve clearing your cache. Normally, the cache is helpful for Outlook, as it stores temporary files for faster loading. But when it becomes corrupted or overloaded, it can lead to a whole host of problems.
Clearing your cache won't delete anything important — all your emails, calendar events and contacts will remain intact. Doing so forces Outlook to create new copies of your emails, fixing sync problems and bringing you the most up-to-date version of your inbox.
Fix Your message can't be displayed right now on Outlook's desktop client
The steps for clearing Outlook's program cache vary slightly across PC and Mac.
On a Windows PC
- 
Close Outlook completely.
- 
Press Win + R on your keyboard to open the Run dialog.
- 
Paste the following file path, then hit Enter: %localappdata%MicrosoftOutlookRoamCache
- 
Select all files in the RoamCache folder and delete them by right-clicking and selecting Delete, or with the Delete key.
On macOS
- 
Open Outlook.
- 
In the upper toolbar, click Tools and then Accounts.
- 
Select your account on the left panel.
- 
Click the three dots and select Reset Account, then confirm the reset.
If this solution doesn't work for your desktop client, you can also try uninstalling and reinstalling the Outlook app.
How to fix Your message can't be displayed right now error in Outlook Web
The method to clear your cache and cookies depends on the browser you're using. You can erase your entire log of website data, but that will log you out of all websites, which isn't convenient. Instead, it's best to clear this data only for the Outlook site. This can take an extra step, but is worth it.
In Microsoft Edge
First, if you want to only clear data on your current device and not all devices where you're signed into Edge, make sure to disable sync:
- 
Click the three dots at the top-right, then select Settings.
- 
Select Profiles, then Sync. Turn off the syncing options. Make sure to re-enable these when you're done.
Then, to clear your Outlook cookies:
- Open the Outlook website.
- Click the Lock icon in the address bar, then choose Cookies and site data > Cookies.
- Select each of the Outlook cookies under Allowed, then click Remove.
- Refresh the page and sign back in.
If this doesn't work, try clearing all site data:
- With Outlook on the web still open, pPress F12 and choose Open DevTools in the popup.
- Click the Plus icon along the top and choose Application.
- On the left menu under Application, click Storage.
- Check the boxes under Clear site data, then choose Clear selected.
- Refresh the page and sign back in.
In Google Chrome
- 
Press F12 to open Developer Tools while you're on the Outlook site.
- 
With that panel open, right-click the Refresh button to the left of the address bar and choose Empty Cache and Hard Reload.
If this doesn't fix the problem, the Edge steps above work nearly the same in Chrome. Click the Site information icon to the left of the address bar, followed by Cookies and site data > Manage on-device site data. Use the trash can icon for each entry here. Then refresh and sign back in.
In Firefox
- 
While on the Outlook page, click the Shield icon to the left of the address bar.
- 
Click Clear cookies and site data, then confirm with Clear once more.
- Refresh the page and sign back in.
In Safari
- 
From the top toolbar, select Safari, then Settings.
- 
Open the Privacy section, then hit Manage Website Data.
- 
Search for Outlook using the search bar, then select its entries and choose Remove.
- 
Refresh the page and sign back in.
In case these steps don't fix your problem, check your browser extensions. Adblockers, privacy tools and similar might interfere with Outlook's operations. Try using your mail in another browser; if it works, the problem lies with your current one.

Bharatiya Kisan Union leader Rakesh Tikait on Monday (September 14, 2026) asked farmers and villagers protesting over their pending demands in Gautam Buddh Nagar to continue their agitation, saying "struggle is the only option" left before them.
Addressing protesting farmers at the offices of the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (YEIDA), Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority (GNIDA) and Noida Authority, Mr. Tikait assured them of his organisation's support and urged them to remain at the protest sites.
"If you cannot enter the office of your local authority, meet officials or raise your issues, are you a hostage or a prisoner? If farmers cannot meet their own officials, struggle is the only option left before them," Mr. Tikait said.
The farmers have been seeking developed residential plots and enhanced compensation for land acquired for development projects. Their demands include 10% developed 'abadi' plots in lieu of acquired land and an additional 64% compensation, besides greater flexibility in using residential plots and more 'abadi' land in villages.
The Bharatiya Kisan Union (BKU) national spokesperson alleged that the administration was preventing farmers from holding protests and meeting officials, leaving them with no alternative but to continue their agitation.
"Whatever they do now, they will have to struggle. I will stand with these people. My support is with them. I tell you to stay here and continue your protest," he said.
Mr. Tikait, a prominent face of the anti-farm laws agitation in 2020-21, said that earlier farmer protests could often be resolved through dialogue as the government also responded positively to such efforts. "But that situation no longer exists. Now people will have to struggle. The time has come when people have to take the path of struggle," he said.
Mr. Tikait met groups of protesting farmers at the three authority offices, sat with them on the protest stage and assured them of the BKU's support.
BKU national general secretary Pawan Khatan earlier said farmers had held meetings and conducted village-to-village outreach ahead of the September 14 Kisan Mahapanchayat under Tikait's leadership.

Following the 25th-anniversary commemoration of the Sept. 11 attacks, news media outlets reported U.S. President Donald Trump planned to fly to Ireland for the weekend to take in the Irish Open at Trump International Golf Club in Doonbeg.
Snopes received a reader's email asking, "Is it true that in Ireland in flight path for Shannon airport is a F*** Trump message in someone's yard?" The reader attached an image of the alleged sign — apparently captured from a high-angle position, similar to that of a drone — showing a grassy field, with the "U" in the first word marked with an asterisk.
A reverse image search found users sharing the same image on Bluesky, Facebook, Threads and TikTok (archived), some also claiming the sign appeared along the flight path into Shannon Airport in County Clare.
(@electra75 via Threads)
Snopes could not independently verify the sign's authenticity as of this writing, but did note a report about the image from CorkBeo, a publication primarily covering matters involving Ireland's County Cork. We reached out to the White House to request comment about the subject matter and will update this article if we receive further information.
The CorkBeo article cited as its source a video that Irish personality Ray Foley posted on Sept. 9, interviewing a woman who said she asked her husband to help prepare the sign for Trump's trip.
Foley's post says the woman, not identified by name, sent a message and the image to him, saying she prepared a "warm welcome" on the flight path into Shannon Airport "for the guest this weekend" — referencing Trump. "We've already had a few black helicopter flybys," the message apparently read.
Speaking about her husband, whom she identified as Paul, the woman reportedly said the following:
I've been troubling him for a long time to do this because we knew he [Trump] was gonna be comin' and I just said, "Come on, come on, keep needlin', and keep putting the idea in his head," so, I think he just gave up and said, "Come on, we'll do it."
We contacted a Foley representative with Today FM's owner, Bauer Media Audio Ireland, to ask for contact information pertaining to the people who created the supposed sign and will add more details if we receive a response.
BBC reported Air Force One, with Trump onboard, would fly into Dublin Airport on Sept. 12, and into Shannon Airport later the same day. CorkBeo's article featured news of a second protest sign that appeared in Dublin, reading "No Kings," as well as mentioning Gaza, Iran and ICE. Reuters published a photo confirming the Dublin sign's authenticity.
