A probe has been ordered by Bhopal Police Commissioner Sanjay Kumar, a day after at least four MBBS intern doctors suffered injuries due to water cannons that were used against them during their protest in the campus of government-run Gandhi Medical College (GMC) to demand a hike in their stipend.
On Monday (September 7, 2026), hundreds of interns of the GMC, Bhopal, protested at their campus over their longstanding demand that their stipend be increased from the current ₹14,437 to ₹30,000. However, as they planned a march to the Chief Minister’s residence, the police used water cannons on the protestors, visuals of which appeared on the internet.
The protestors also alleged that as they continued their march later in the day, the police also resorted to baton charge on them near the campus. The march was stopped less than 2 kilometres from the CM house, prompting them to launch a sit-in at the site.
The sit-in in Bhopal’s Kamla Park area continued through the night and on Tuesday (September 8) even as they boycotted the OPD and routine operation theatre (OT) services, while emergency services remained operational. Services were also interrupted at Gwalior’s Gajra Raja Medical College in support of the protest.
Four interns injured in the police action
Speaking to The Hindu, Siddhartha Kumar Rai, undergraduate student wing president of the Junior Doctors’ Association (JDA), Madhya Pradesh, said that at least four interns got seriously injured in the police action, including one person suffering a broken arm and another an eye injury.
“It was a completely peaceful protest inside the campus but still the interns who perform 36-hour-long duties and contribute the most in handling the heavy patient load at government hospitals were treated like goons by the police. They even targeted the girl interns who were standing on the side,” he said.
Meanwhile, various other doctors’ bodies in the State have also come out in support of the interns’ protest while condemning the police action.
Mr. Rai said that if a written assurance was not given by Tuesday night, the JDA and various other bodies will boycott medical services across the State from Wednesday (September 9).
Dr. Kavita N. Singh, Dean and CEO, GMC, Bhopal, also slammed the use of force in a letter to Commissioner Kumar while seeking an inquiry into the matter and action against responsible officers.
“Water cannon was used and lathicharge was done on the intern students at the emergency gate in which two students were injured.
Taking such action against intern students on the hospital campus without prior notice is completely inappropriate,” she wrote.
In an order, Mr. Kumar said that the matter was brought to attention by Deputy Chief Minister and Health Minister Rajendra Shukla and that Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP), Zone 2, Vikas Sahwal has been appointed to conduct an “impartial investigation of the whole incident”.
“It has been brought to the notice by Shri Rajendra Shukla, Deputy Chief Minister, that during the protest of intern doctors in Bhopal on September 7, 2026, the police sprayed water using water cannon near the gate of Hamidia Hospital, due to which some doctors were injured,” the order read.
Mr. Rai also claimed that Madhya Pradesh ranked 28th in the country in the amount of stipend given to MBBS interns, after the Uttar Pradesh increasing the amount from ₹12,000 to ₹25,000 in August.
“But in terms of MBBS fee at government colleges, we are at the third position with about ₹1.15 lakh. How is this fair,” he asked.
Meanwhile, Mr. Shukla also held a meeting with senior officials and the management of the GMC to discuss the issue and interns’ demand and said that a resolution will be reached soon.
“I am aware of the issue raised by intern doctors in Bhopal regarding an increase in stipends. The expectations and problems of young doctors in the state are being taken seriously. I am in constant touch with representatives of the intern doctors on this matter,” he wrote on X.
“Our effort is to engage in positive discussions with all parties and arrive at an appropriate and practical solution to this issue. Young doctors play a vital role in strengthening the health services of the state, and the government is sensitive to their rightful expectations. Following discussions and necessary deliberations, appropriate and necessary decisions will be taken in this regard,” he added.

Over 20 feared trapped after bus plunges 30 feet into Tamil Nadu river
There were 32 passengers on board the bus, of whom more than 20 were feared trapped inside following the accident.
More than 20 passengers were feared trapped after a Tamil Nadu government bus overturned and fell into the Azhutha Kanni river near Vettaikarankulam in Tenkasi district on Sunday, police said.
The bus, operating on the Tenkasi-Tirunelveli route, overturned and plunged into the river, which is around 30 feet below the road level.
There were 32 passengers on board the bus, of whom more than 20 were feared trapped inside following the accident.
Tenkasi fire and rescue personnel rushed to the spot after receiving information and launched a rescue operation.

17 injured in the accident
Police said 17 passengers were injured in the accident. The driver, Sivasakthi, 49, sustained severe injuries and was shifted to Tirunelveli Government Medical College Hospital for further treatment.
The other injured passengers were shifted to Tenkasi Government Hospital.
Courtallam Police are investigating the incident.
Meanwhile, in a separate incident in Visakhapatnam, a bus caught fire at Dwaraka Bus Station on Saturday after all passengers had safely disembarked.
APSRTC Visakhapatnam Regional Manager Appala Naidu said the bus, belonging to the Nellore-1 Depot, had departed at 5 pm on Saturday and arrived at Dwaraka Bus Station at around 7 am on Sunday.
Naidu said all passengers had safely alighted and parcel services had been completely unloaded before the bus left the station.
The drivers were taking the empty bus towards the Waltair Depot when the driver noticed smoke coming from the vehicle and pulled over.
“The driver noticed smoke coming out of the vehicle, immediately pulled over, and informed the local Assistant Engineer, Assistant Manager and Depot Manager. Fire engines were alerted right away, but despite prompt action, the bus engine and vehicle were completely gutted in the fire,” Naidu said.

Indonesian rescuers were searching on Sunday for 140 people from a passenger ship that was earlier reported missing in the Java Sea after 103 others were evacuated, one of whom died, a search and rescue agency official said.
A passenger ship carrying more than 240 people was reported missing after losing contact during bad weather in the Java Sea early on Sunday, the country’s search and rescue agency said.
The Virgo Transport 8 ship set sail on Saturday from the East Java city of Surabaya to the South Kalimantan city of Banjarmasin before losing contact.
I Putu Sudayana, the head of the agency’s Banjarmasin office, said in a video statement that 103 people had been evacuated using different ships and some of them would be taken to an East Java port.
Rescuers launched a search, deploying a team, ships and a helicopter toward the passenger vessel’s last known position, he said, without stating what happened to the ship.
The search and rescue office in the city of Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan, which is located on Borneo island, said it received a report two hours after contact was lost with the Virgo Transport 8 at about 2am on Sunday.
“The ship’s operator reported the incident to authorities after receiving information that the vessel had encountered bad weather,” Sudayana, who heads the search and rescue office, said in a video briefing.
Indonesia, an archipelago of 17,000 islands, relies heavily on ferries as a key mode of transportation, with sea routes more affordable and readily available than air travel.
However, safety standards are not always rigorously enforced, resulting in a relatively high accident rate.

In Summary
- The Redmi Turbo 5 sees the Redmi brand return to a higher price point. It had earlier released the K series in this segment.
- The Redmi Turbo 5 follows Redmi’s classic formula of offering very good specs at surprisingly affordable prices. Its highlights are a powerful chip and a large Silicon Carbon battery.
- Priced at Rs 41,999, the Redmi Turbo 5 is one of the best options for those looking for something close to a budget flagship in an era of rapidly rising prices.
Redmi is mainly known for its budget-friendly devices, mostly in the mid- and lower-mid segment. It has occasionally released slightly more expensive devices, most notably in its K series, but has then gone back to the comfort of the Redmis and Redmi Notes. Now, as phone prices get on an upward-heading escalator, Redmi is getting back into the higher price zone with the Redmi Turbo 5. It comes with a starting price of Rs. 41,999, and while that may seem a bit on the premium side for a Redmi smartphone, it brings an equally premium spec sheet to the table. But can it help Redmi stretch beyond Note-land? Let’s find out!
Table of Contents
Redmi Turbo 5 design and appearance: Classy, yet not-so-loud appearance
The Redmi Turbo 5 does not come with a radically new design – it looks very similar to its cousin, the Poco X8 Pro. And that is a good thing. The phone has all the design elements that make up a trendy smartphone in today’s day and age – a tall, display dominated front which is surrounded by razor thin bezels, a flat back with two circular camera rings jutting out just a little parked on the top left side, and has those flat sides that have become an essential part of a modern day smartphone’s anatomy.
While not out of the box, the Turbo 5 still has a few distinct design touches that catch attention, the kind that are not obvious or scream for attention, but do not get lost completely either. The right side of the back comes with a thick vertical strip filled with very dainty checkered patterns, and the cameras seem like two independent lenses stacked together, but there is a subtle capsule outline encasing them. The two camera lenses also have LED rings inside them, which is a nice conversation starter.
We received the Turbo White variant of the smartphone, which has a red Redmi logo near the base of the back. The cameras and the power/lock button also come with a very distinct red accent. These subtle touches make the design of the Redmi Turbo 5 give it a personality of sorts, making it stand out in the crowd. The back comes with a matte finish, which keeps smudges and scratches at bay and keeps the phone relatively clean. The metallic frame (a pleasant surprise at this price) is home to a handful of features as well. The top carries an infrared port while the base holds a SIM card tray, a USB Type-C port, and a speaker grille. The left side is bare while the right one bears the volume rocker and the power lock button.
Although relatively light for the size of the battery it carries (more about that later), the phone is not exactly light. It weighs 204 grams, and you can feel the weight in hand and even when the phone is in your pocket. At 157.5 mm, the Redmi Turbo 5 falls somewhere between large (160 mm and above) and compact phones (153 mm and below). It is 75.2 mm wide and, at 8.18 mm, is impressively slim, again considering the size of its battery. It is quite a sturdy phone with Gorilla Glass 7i protection on its front and back, and with IP68 and IP69K ratings for dust and water resistance, which means it can easily survive a fall in the water.
At first glance, the Redmi Turbo 5 might seem routine, but give it more attention, and little details start to pop up, and you start appreciating it for its classy, yet not-so-loud appearance.
Redmi Turbo 5 Specs: Ticks a surprising number of boxes
At a time when brands are cutting spec corners, the Redmi Turbo 5 ticks a surprising number of boxes. The phone is powered by a MediaTek Dimensity 8500 Ultra processor, which is considered to be in the budget flagship zone, and is paired with 8 GB and 12 GB RAM options and 256 GB of storage. What’s more, the 12 GB RAM variant comes with LPDDR5X RAM, and the storage on both variants is UFS 4.1. On paper, this is a very powerful setup for the price, which can not only run your everyday smartphone tasks but even handle high-end gaming.
The phone comes with a 6.59-inch AMOLED full HD+ (2756 x 1268) display with 120 Hz refresh rate and a peak brightness of 3500 nits, which can actually cover as much as 25 per cent of the display, instead of being isolated to a tiny section. Photography is handled by a dual camera setup on the back comprising a 50 megapixel Sony IMX882 main sensor with OIS, and an 8 megapixel ultrawide sensor, while a 20 megapixel sensor on the front handles selfies.
The Turbo 5 also packs in some very impressive battery numbers – it brings a sizable 7540 mAh Silicon Carbon battery (a rarity at this price, actually at any price) with support for 100W charging and 27W reverse charging. Also on board are stereo speakers, an in-display fingerprint scanner, and an IR blaster. Like all Redmi devices, the Turbo 5 also runs on Android 16 topped with Xiaomi’s HyperOS 3. Xiaomi promises four years of software and six years of security updates.
In sheer spec terms, this is one of the best specced devices out there in its segment. Some might find the display a little small, but the power of that processor and the RAM and storage options will attract gamers on a budget.
Redmi Turbo 5 Performance: A smooth, powerful operator
The Redmi Turbo 5’s speedy processor+ RAM+ storage set up, reflects in its performance as well. The phone sails smoothly through everyday duties. It moves from app to app smoothly, handles multi-tasking without a hiccup, keeps going through intense social media scrolls, and binge sessions on OTT. The phone can also handle high-end games like Call of Duty and BGMI at 120 fps for long-ish sessions. Although it does get warm while going through power-hungry tasks, the temperature comes down quickly enough.
The AMOLED display with a 120 Hz refresh rate does not disappoint. It delivers a very rich contrast with vibrant colors and is bright enough not to dull down against a very harsh sun either. The 120 Hz refresh rate kept scrolling through social media breezy. The in-display fingerprint scanner works smoothly as well. This, combined with the loud and clear stereo speakers, makes the phone a multimedia master. We did not face any call drops or connectivity issues with the phone either.
Redmi Turbo 5 Cameras: One sensor show (censor the others)
Cameras are not the forte of the Redmi Turbo 5. There are three sensors on the phone, but all the photography weight rests on the 50-megapixel main sensor’s shoulders. This performs well in daylight conditions, capturing a good amount of detail and producing sharp images, so much so that the photos look decent even after a little zoom-in. The colors seem slightly more vibrant than reality but never to a point of looking unnatural. The details do take a very marginal hit in low light, but the presence of OIS helps, and Night mode on the device also improves results a fair bit. A number of other modes are built right into the native camera app, which offer a lot of scope for creative photography.
The 8-megapixel ultrawide sensor is capable of capturing a wider area, but it does not really do an impressive job. The colors remain nice and vibrant, but the details take a nose dive, resulting in images that look noisier, especially when compared to the main sensor. Matters only get worse as the light dims down. The sensor is usable and will allow you to take some quick snaps for social media in good light conditions, but do not pin your photography hopes on it. The 20-megapixel sensor on the front delivers social media-ready snaps but has the tendency to smooth out skin texture even with no ‘beauty mode’ on. The colors also lean towards being a little oversaturated, but you can get good casual snaps, and video calls are handled well.
The main camera supports 4K video at 60 fps, but the other two cameras are limited to 1080p at 60 fps. The video performance of the main camera sensor is good in daylight and even in low-light conditions, but the others miss the mark a bit. Overall, the 50-megapixel camera is the star of the Redmi Turbo 5’s camera show, while the other two are just supporting staff.
Redmi Turbo 5 software and UI: Very nice HyperOS, but loaded with third-party apps
The Redmi Turbo 5 runs on HyperOS 3. Now, HyperOS has been one of the most intuitive, simple, and functional Android skins since its MIUI days, and while that still largely remains true, the phone comes loaded with a plethora of third-party apps. This really makes the experience feel very cluttered and might even seem overwhelming to those new to the UI. Most of these third-party apps can be uninstalled, thankfully.
That said, features like Xiaomi Interconnectivity that not only allow you to connect your smartphone with other HyperOS products but with other gadgets as well, letting you create a hybrid ecosystem, give HyperOS its productivity edge. Top this with add-ons like Hyper Island (similar to Dynamic Island on the iPhone), and AI features like AI Translate, writing assist, call transcription, and a range of customizations, and HyperOS comes across as a very functionality-forward UI. The LED rings around the camera sensors that light up when you get notifications or calls were actually very handy, even while being a nice party trick as well.
Redmi Turbo 5 Battery: Lasts for days, gets charged in a jiffy
The phone’s massive 7540 mAh battery can see you through even the heaviest work days. Emails, messaging, gaming, photography- we did all of that and more with the smartphone, and it still had some juice left even after a day. If you are someone who does not push their device as much, the phone would easily see off more than two days on a single charge. It comes with 100W fast charging support with a 100W brick in the box, which means you get a fully charged phone in slightly over an hour, while the phone goes from 0-50 percent in about 30 minutes. This makes the Redmi Turbo 5 a device that will not only last for day(s) but will also get charged in a jiffy. The reverse charging feature is quite handy too and charges our TWS at a very decent speed.
Redmi Turbo 5 Price: Typically Redmi!
The Redmi Turbo 5 is available in two RAM variants – 8 GB and 12 GB, while the storage remains 256 GB for both options. Although the phone was initially launched at Rs 37,999, this price has since been revised, given rising costs of inputs. The 8 GB/ 256 GB version of the phone is now priced at Rs. 41,999, while the 12 GB/ 256 GB version is priced at Rs. 46,999.
It might have a much higher starting price than the Redmi Note series, but the Redmi Turbo 5 brings a solid spec sheet to the table at a price tag that is typically Redmi. While there are other devices in its price range, at the time of writing, none quite match its price-to-spec equation.
Perhaps the one that comes closest is its own cousin, the Poco X8 Pro, which comes with a similar processor and a similarly sized display at Rs 39,999, but has a smaller battery. Devices like the OnePlus Nord 6 come with a comparable Qualcomm Snapdragon 8s Gen 4 chip, but are more expensive at Rs 46,999, while the recently launched Vivo S2 brings a sleeker design and bigger display to the table at Rs 39,999 but loses out in terms of processor muscle.
Redmi Turbo 5 Review Verdict: A phone that does everything well
It might come with a higher price tag, but the Redmi Turbo 5 is a typical Redmi smartphone in more than one aspect. It delivers a very consistent performance across multiple segments, making it one of the most reliable and powerful options at its price point (typical Redmi!). Its gaming and general performance are both quite smooth; the main camera delivers good snaps, its battery is perhaps its biggest USP, and the display combined with the stereo speakers make it an entertainment master. The price tag is a little higher than some might expect, but the Redmi Turbo 5 is a device for those who are looking for a very good everyday phone that does almost everything well.
- Smart design, sturdy build
- Gorgeous display
- Very good speakers
- Long battery that charges swiftly too
- Good gaming and multimedia performance
- Smooth overall performance
- Ultrawide camera is average
- Bloatware in UI

In a shocking incident, a Kargil War veteran was allegedly attacked with an iron rod in Gurugram, leaving him with serious head injuries and a fractured hand.
According to an NDTV report, retired Group Captain Amit Kumar Gupta, who was part of the Indian Air Force's 'Op Safed Sagar' team in 1999, was attacked unprovoked by a parking attendant at Magnum Global Park in Gurugram.
In his police complaint, Gupta alleged that the attendant had also threatened to kill him. He also accused the police of not helping him and alleged that the hospital submitted a false report.
Amit Gupta has gone for a family dinner at Gonzo restaurant at Magnum Global Park on Thursday night at around 8 pm.
After dropping his family at the restaurant, he was searching for a parking space, but was directed to different locations — the valet, basement, and multilevel parking — by the parking staff who eventually refused to park his car, Gupta said in his complaint.
At one point, while he was trying to reverse his car, a parking attendant allegedly hit his windshield in an attempt to break it.
Recounting the horrifying incident, Gupta told NDTV: “When I came out of the car and protested, the attendant brought an iron rod and hit me twice, once on my hand and then on my head. I was drenched in blood.”
The accused also allegedly made life threats to Gupta.
Amit Gupta alleged that neither the security personnel nor the other parking staff present at the spot came to his rescue. He said that he had even dialled the police helpline, but they didn't come for another half hour.
Eventually, a chef intervened, saving his life.
"The attack was sudden and unprovoked. I couldn't even defend myself," he recounted.
The attack left Gupta with serious injuries to his head and elbow. According to NDTV, he was rushed to Medanta Hospital, where he underwent surgery to fuse his elbow bone with plates.
The veteran has also accused the hospital of submitting a false MLC (medico-legal case) report, which has no mention of the bleeding and elbow injury. “I am not getting any support from the police,” he added.
Demanding strict action against the accused, Gupta, in his submission to the police, said an FIR must be registered against the accused for an attempt to murder and causing grievous hurt.
In 1999, the Indian Air Force launched 'Operation Safed Sagar' to dislodge Pakistani intruders from occupied positions across the icy heights of Kargil.

- The claim that attendees of the 2026 Republican National Convention in Dallas, Texas, caused an outage of popular gay dating app Grindr circulated online in September 2026.
- The rumor stems from incident reports shared on social media, taken from a third-party service called Downdetector during the time of the event. However, the incidents were not isolated to Dallas, and Grindr itself did not report any major outages connected to the event.
- A spokesperson for Grindr told Snopes, "Grindr has not experienced recent outages. Third party sources that often make these claims rely on unreliable data such as self-reporting, while Grindr reports outages directly on its status page." The status page showed no outages in August or September 2026.
- While some users may have had trouble with the service on Sept. 9 and 10, 2026, including in and around the area where the RNC was being held, we were unable to independently verify that the reported errors were authentic or that they were caused specifically by RNC attendees.
With high-stakes midterms looming in November 2026, the Republican National Convention took place in Dallas, Texas, on Sept. 9 and 10, 2026. Rumors spread that the convention's attendees were causing an outage of the popular gay dating app Grindr.
People on social media sites shared a purported screenshot that showed a map depicting hotspots of Grindr outages across the country, with the brightest spot focused on Dallas.
The popularity of the rumor led many Snopes readers to reach out via email and social media, asking if the claim was true.
We weren't able to independently verify claims of Grindr outages in Dallas, so we've left this claim unrated. The screenshots appeared to be taken from Downdetector, a third-party service that tracks outages of popular services, and did not show signs of fabrication or misleading editing.
According to Downdetector, users did report incidents at the time and location in question, but the incidents reported on Sept. 9 and 10 were not limited to Dallas or even Texas. There was also no way to confirm that the reports reflected real issues with the app, as Downdetector does not require users to submit any proof.
Grindr itself did not report any outages during that time.
A spokesperson for Grindr told Snopes via email: "Grindr has not experienced recent outages. Third party sources that often make these claims rely on unreliable data such as self-reporting, while Grindr reports outages directly on its status page."
The company's status page showed no outages or incidents in August or September 2026.
Downdetector tracks data for the prior 24 hours and does not archive its history.
Snopes first checked Downdetector's page for Grindr on Sept. 10, 2026. It showed a spike of reported outages on Sept. 9 around 8:49 p.m., with the highest number of reports clocked at 460.
Grindr outage report on Sept. 10, 2026. (Downdetector)
When we checked Downdetector on Sept. 11, the past 24 hours showed a peak of only 73 reports around 3:18 p.m. on Sept. 10.
Grindr outage report on Sept. 11, 2026. (Downdetector)
The incident heat map provided by Downdetector, which we first checked on Sept. 10, showed the highest concentration of outages in Dallas and Austin, Texas, but also indicated reports were being submitted in other major cities like New York, Boston and Chicago.
Grindr outage map on Sept. 10, 2026. (Downdetector)
A look at the same map one day later showed lower concentrations of reports of problems in the same cities.
(Grindr outage map on Sept. 11, 2026. (Downdetector))
The page explains that Downdetector "calculates a baseline volume of typical problem reports for each service monitored" based on an average over six months, and "only reports an incident when the number of problem reports is significantly higher than the baseline."
Further, Downdetector allows users reporting the issues to comment on the page. During the period of Snopes' review for this claim, multiple comments on Grindr's Downdetector page referenced the RNC with comments like, "Convention in Dallas, as always." There was no indication those comments came from people genuinely experiencing connection issues in Dallas.
So while it appeared that some users may have had trouble with the service on Sept. 9 and 10, 2026, including in and around the area where the RNC was being held, there was not enough evidence to conclude without a doubt that the reported errors were entirely authentic or that they were indeed caused specifically by attendees at the RNC.
We reached out to Ookla, the parent company of Downdetector, for further comment and will update this article if we hear back.
For further reading, we've investigated similar claims about Grindr, such as rumors of alleged Grindr outages near Charlie Kirk's memorial in September 2025.

Bears, Bills and Ravens win on record-breaking Sunday
- Published
The NFL is back with a bang.
After kicking off the season with a Super Bowl rematch and a trip to Australia, week one continued with a record-breaking Sunday.
The Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Ravens showed why they are favourites to win the AFC Conference, and the Chicago Bears made a statement as they racked up 59 points.
Those wins contributed to an NFL record for the most points scored on the opening Sunday of the season since the league merger in 1970.
Here's what you need to know from the opening weekend.
Bills look sharp under new coach
The Bills changed their head coach in a bid to finally reach the Super Bowl with star quarterback Josh Allen, promoting offensive co-ordinator Joe Brady to the top job.
His first game was a big test, coming against last season's meanest defence, and the lead changed hands eight times in a thriller at the Houston Texans.
Running back David Montgomery scored three touchdowns on his Houston debut, but Allen ran in two touchdowns and passed for two more.
The 2024 season's Most Valuable Player was almost intercepted as he launched a hopeful pass into the endzone with less than two minutes remaining.
But on the next play 30-year-old Allen held his nerve with a 34-yard throw to Joshua Palmer that clinched a 36-31 win.
Buffalo's first five games are against potential Super Bowl contenders, so they needed to hit the ground running.
Bears bullish after record opener
After missing last season's play-offs the Baltimore Ravens brought an end to John Harbaugh's 18-year tenure as head coach, and they made a flying start under successor Jesse Minter.
Zay Flowers, who became the NFL's fourth highest-paid wide receiver in the off-season, made five catches for a career-high 150 yards and a touchdown in the first half alone at the Indianapolis Colts.
Derrick Henry also scored twice before half-time to move into third on the all-time list for rushing touchdowns, then added another as the Ravens cruised to a 41-23 win.
But there was concern for Baltimore as Flowers and rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane missed the second half with hamstring and wrist injuries respectively.
The Ravens' impressive win was soon eclipsed by the Chicago Bears, who were level with the Carolina Panthers at 31-31 midway through the third quarter before romping to victory.
Running back D'Andre Swift finished with three touchdowns in a 59-37 road win - the highest-scoring week one game in NFL history and Chicago's highest score since 1980.
After leading the Bears to their first division title in seven years last season, head coach Ben Johnson has set some lofty targets.
"We want to be the highest scoring. We want to have the most wins. We want to win Super Bowls," he said.
Genuine belief in Giants
Harbaugh is now in charge of a promising young roster at the New York Giants, and his first game came on a poignant night at the MetLife Stadium, which hosted the football World Cup final in July.
Two days after the 25th anniversary of 9/11, the Giants honoured New York's first responders and those impacted by the attacks with a series of tributes before Sunday's primetime game.
The Giants then produced a convincing 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys, with second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart passing for 230 yards and three touchdowns, while fit-again running back Cam Skattebo rushed for another.
It was a balanced team performance with a disciplined defence, a trademark of Harbaugh's team throughout his time in Baltimore.
With the New York Knicks ending their long wait for an NBA championship this year, there is genuine belief that the Giants can also get back in play-off contention.
Cardinals stun Chargers
The Arizona Cardinals have been tipped by many to finish with the NFL's worst record, while the Los Angeles Chargers are seen as play-off contenders.
But the Chargers were humbled on their own turf at SoFi Stadium, which will host Super Bowl 61 in February.
The Cardinals are trying to make a fresh start having brought in Mike LaFleur as head coach and released quarterback Kyler Murray, and they dominated possession in a 26-14 win.
Murray, who went on to earn the starting role with the Minnesota Vikings, made a wretched start at home to the Green Bay Packers, coached by LaFleur's older brother Matt.
Murray's first pass with the Vikings was intercepted, and the former first overall draft pick then suffered a concussion before being replaced by veteran Carson Wentz.
Despite falling 22-10 down late in the third quarter, the Vikings fought back to win 39-22, with Justin Jefferson claiming two well-taken touchdowns and a two-point conversion.
The Vikings have had nine starting quarterbacks since Jefferson was named offensive player of the year for 2022, and the wide receiver looked back to his best.
Revamped Bengals look the real deal
Although the Cincinnati Bengals have one of the NFL's most potent offences, they have been let down by their defence in the past three seasons.
The front office tried to remedy that in the off-season, and the revamped defence was impressive in their opener against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Three of last season's 11 defeats came despite scoring at least 34 points, and again the Bengals had little trouble scoring against the Bucs.
This time their defence did their job too, though, recording four sacks and forcing four fumbles. All four were recovered by Cincinnati, with one returned for a defensive touchdown in a 33-27 home win.
If the Bengals can maintain that consistency - and quarterback Joe Burrow avoids another injury-hit season - they could have realistic hope of returning to the Super Bowl, having played the last time the big game was held in LA in 2022.

The US government launched at least three previously unreported investigations into trading on the prediction market Polymarket, according to documents obtained by WIRED through a Freedom of Information Act request.
Voting records from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the federal agency that regulates prediction markets, shed new light on how the government approaches these investigations. In early May, CFTC chairman Michael Selig approved an order allowing the agency’s enforcement division to launch a private investigation into potential insider trading on Polymarket event contracts related to pardons issued by former president Joseph Biden. The order granted permission to take testimony, obtain subpoenas, administer oaths, and require the production of documents in the course of the investigation.
The documents obtained by WIRED did not specify which trades were under suspicion, but the order came several weeks after an NPR report on a suspicious Polymarket trader who netted over $300,000 on pardon-related markets in the final days of the Biden administration. The trader correctly wagered that the former president would issue preemptive pardons to a number of prominent MAGA critics, including former US representatives Liz Cheney and Adam Kinzinger, and US senator Adam Schiff.
At the end of May, Selig approved another investigation order. This time, the topic was “Iran event contracts” on Polymarket. As with the Biden pardon documents, the investigation order did not provide details, but it came two weeks after 60 Minutes aired a report on a network of suspicious Polymarket accounts that made $2.4 million on Iran-related trades, with a 98 percent win rate.
“If these investigations are being prompted solely by press reports of potential violations of the Commodities Exchange Act, that’s a significant sign of weakness in this regulatory scheme,” says Joseph Konizeski, a former chief trial attorney in the CFTC’s division of enforcement. The agency has come under fire in the second Trump era for its perceived friendliness to the prediction market industry.
In July, Selig greenlit a third investigation, this time focused on suspected insider trading on Google-themed Polymarket event contracts. In an email exchange included in the documents obtained by WIRED, Paul Hayeck, the acting director of the CFTC’s department of enforcement, noted that the investigation would focus on “additional individuals who may have engaged in insider trading related to Google’s 2025 Year in Search Ranking.” Hayeck wrote that the Southern District of New York is conducting a “parallel investigation.” He specified that the CFTC's investigation would be separate from the ongoing case against Michele Spagnuolo, a Google engineer accused of insider trading.
SDNY declined to comment. Google declined to comment. It pointed WIRED to a statement it released in June noting that Spagnuolo was no longer with the company. The CFTC did not respond to requests for comment and questions about the status of the investigations.
“While we do not comment on specific investigations, we regularly refer matters to law enforcement and support ongoing investigations as part of our commitment to protecting the integrity of our markets,” Olivia Chalos, deputy chief legal officer at Polymarket, told WIRED in an email.
The CFTC is also reportedly investigating Polymarket itself. The company, which had its flagship platform banned from the United States in 2022, was permitted to launch a US-regulated version with a narrower set of markets in late 2025. It recently underwent a fundraising round led by Donald Trump Jr.’s venture capital firm, 1789 Capital, which valued the company at $21 billion.
The CFTC has also launched investigations into potential insider trading on Kalshi, Polymarket’s archrival, in the past. According to The New York Times, Kalshi has referred at least 32 cases to the agency. The CFTC fined former US representative George Santos $35,000 for his behavior related to a Kalshi contract about whether he would attend Trump’s 2026 State of the Union address.
Kalshi issued its first-ever lifetime ban to Santos for violating its rules on market manipulation for the same behavior, and also fined him just over $71,000. Santos was not criminally charged.
So far, two arrests have been made stemming from Polymarket insider trading investigations. In April, federal authorities arrested a US special forces officer who prosecutors say used classified information to make more than $400,000 in profits on event contracts related to the capture of former Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro. And in May, Spagnuolo, who allegedly made over $1.2 million on insider trades, was arrested while traveling to New York. In both cases, the CFTC filed civil charges, and the Department of Justice filed criminal fraud charges. Both men are fighting back by arguing that Polymarket trades are a form of betting and not subject to commodities law.
It’s unclear if the Department of Justice has launched parallel investigations into the Iran War or Biden pardon contracts. The DOJ did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
A former CFTC staffer tells WIRED that parallel criminal investigations are likely, “given the significance of the matters.”
Additional reporting by Maddy Varner.

Uganda's King Oyo buried amid calls for unity over his successor
- Published
Uganda's King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, once the world's youngest reigning monarch, was buried on Saturday, days after a row broke out over who would succeed him.
Oyo, 34, who had ruled the traditional kingdom of Tooro in western Uganda since the age of three, died last month while undergoing cancer treatment in the US.
Tooro is one of Uganda's traditional kingdoms. They were abolished in 1967 but restored in the 1990s under President Museveni. Their monarchs are recognised as cultural leaders rather than political rulers.
Thousands of mourners lined the streets as the king's casket was transported to the royal tombs in Fort Portal where a private ceremony took place.
Oyo was just a toddler when he was named as Tooro's king and, according to Guinness World Records, was the world's youngest monarch while he reigned.
TV news presenter Prince Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma, 56, who was named as the next monarch by clan elders, reportedly cast nine coffee beans into Oyo's grave, a ritual signifying the end of one reign and the start of another.
But days earlier, Oyo's family rejected Kijanangoma, the late monarch's cousin, as Tooro's new king.
Oyo's sister, Princess Ruth Komuntale, said the late king had left a will, written in 2022, naming his young son as his successor.
The boy's identity has never been disclosed.
Meanwhile, his mother, Queen Best Kemigisa, said royal guards had been withdrawn from the palace and soldiers deployed. This, she said, restricted the royal family's movement and their ability to receive visitors, describing it as "house arrest".
On Saturday, the Archbishop of the Church of Uganda, Stephen Kazimba Mugalu, urged unity.
"Words spoken in grief can cause pain, division and conflict. It can even destroy the legacy of the king we are mourning," he told mourners.
Uganda's President Yoweri Museveni also called for the matter to be resolved "and to favour unity over division".
The clan overseeing the succession defended its choice of Kijanangoma.
Omusuuga Charles Karumasi, head of the Babiito royal clan, said: "We have done everything in observance of the culture and traditions of Tooro. We must all preserve peace and serenity."

‘Someone gave ₹20 to eat’: BJP's richest Maharashtra MLA Parag Shah turns beggar for a day
Parag Shah, who represents Ghatkopar (East), sought alms and ate food offered to him while sitting by the roadside.
Maharashtra BJP MLA Parag Shah, one of the state’s wealthiest legislators, spent a day on the streets of Mumbai dressed as a beggar, leaving behind his security detail, cars and expensive belongings for the unusual exercise.
Shah, who represents Ghatkopar (East), sought alms and ate food offered to him while sitting by the roadside. A video of the MLA in disguise went viral on social media, initially surprising viewers before details of the act emerged.
The businessman-turned-politician said he undertook the experience on the advice of his Jain spiritual guru Namramuni during the ongoing special month, which is considered significant in Jain religious tradition, news agency PTI reported.
Shah goes undercover as beggar
Following his guru’s advice, Shah stayed away from his security arrangements, vehicles and expensive possessions. He also underwent makeup to ensure people would not recognise him and spent several hours on the streets in the guise of a beggar.
Reflecting on the experience, Shah said it gave him an understanding of how people behave when their social status is not known.
"All the respect and honour, the people who line up to meet you -- the same people, when I go to them, become taller than me. So, that is the reality of life," Shah maintained while recounting his experience.
‘Mumbai city is always ready to help’
Shah said the exercise also showed him the willingness of people in Mumbai to help others.
"Someone gave me ₹20 saying, 'Go baba, eat food'. There was a samosa seller there. I went to him and took a samosa, and he gave it without any charge. I saw one thing, Mumbai city is such that people here are always ready to help one another," Shah recounted.
He said the samosa seller continued to help him even after he said he had no money.
"And that is my own experience'¦ when I told the samosa seller that I did not have money, he still gave me the samosa with a smile. The man was very small, a poor hawker, but without making a face even once, he gave me the samosa," he said.
MLA revisits places after removing disguise
Shah not only collected alms but also consumed the food he received and spent time sitting by the roadside as a beggar. He later shared the experience with his guru and others.
After removing his makeup, Shah returned to some of the places he had visited while in disguise and spoke to the same people again. This allowed him to observe their reactions without them knowing that he was the person they had encountered earlier.
Parag Shah’s wealth and political career
Shah, who is active in the real estate sector, had declared assets worth more than ₹3,383 crore in his affidavit for the 2024 Maharashtra Assembly elections, making him the state’s richest candidate at the time.
The realtor-cum-politician has also previously served as a corporator of the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation.

Relatives and local residents carried the coffins, with 18 displayed together inside the church during the service.

The New Mexico Supreme Court held a ChatGPT-using lawyer in direct contempt of court for submitting a brief with “false testimony from wholly fabricated witnesses,” including fake police testimony and other mistakes. The state’s top court referred the lawyer to a disciplinary board for further proceedings and concluded that he “demonstrated a lack of remorse and a lack of concern for his client.”
Attorney Stephen Aarons “admitted to the Court that he did not verify the factual claims and legal authority in his AI-generated brief before signing it and filing it with the Court, and that he did not inform his client of this failure or that the brief in chief contained multiple factual and legal misrepresentations,” the state Supreme Court said in an order on Wednesday.
Aarons has been a criminal defense lawyer in New Mexico for over 40 years and was hired by a defendant’s family members to appeal a murder conviction. Aaron’s now-former client, Oscar Renee Sandoval, was sentenced to life in prison in February 2025 after being convicted of killing Shiereen Al-Jibury, who was his partner and the mother of his children.
A little over a year ago, in August 2025, Aarons submitted the brief containing fake testimony and other errors. Weeks later, the state of New Mexico filed a motion to strike portions of that brief.
“Respondent admitted to the Court that the brief in chief contained false testimony from wholly fabricated witnesses—Officer Michelle Amarillo, Officer Sanchez, Manal Al-Jibury, and Teresa Marquez,” the court order on Wednesday said.
Lawyer fed trial transcript into ChatGPT
Aarons further admitted submitting “false testimony from Danny Stanton that he received threats,” “false testimony from Linda Stanton about the threats her husband received,” and “false testimony from Mariah Chavez and Teresa Marquez (fabricated witness) regarding the shooter’s clothing and appearance,” according to the order, which said Aarons also “misrepresented legal authority” in citations to previous cases.
Many lawyers have been caught citing fake cases in briefs or inaccurately describing real cases. While Aarons didn’t cite fake cases, he inaccurately described real ones and cited fake testimony.
Aarons told the state Supreme Court at a hearing on August 21 that he fed a computer-generated transcript of the murder trial and other documents related to the case into ChatGPT, which outputted the fake quotes.
“It’s of little comfort to know that my stupidity is what brings us together this afternoon,” Aarons told the court. Aarons admitted his brief quoted “several witnesses who were never called at trial,” another “witness who was called but the brief got the name wrong,” and that his brief inaccurately described precedents.
Aarons indicated that he used a version of ChatGPT powered by the OpenAI o3 model, which was released earlier in 2025. “I assumed that it generated a bulletproof summary of proceedings,” he said at the hearing, explaining that he thought it would be accurate because of how widespread AI use is in the legal and medical fields.
Aarons was barred from appearing before the New Mexico Supreme Court pending the outcome of any disciplinary board investigation and proceedings. He was fined $5,000, to be paid to the State Bar of New Mexico Client Protection Fund, but more penalties could come out of the disciplinary proceedings ordered by the court.
The state Supreme Court ordered the public defender office to appoint a new lawyer for the defendant, struck all previous briefs from the record, and said the case will proceed in the court’s 2026-27 term.
Justice: “You buried your head in the sand”
Justices lambasted Aarons during last month’s hearing. They expressed surprise that Aarons didn’t know AI tools could generate false information and pointed out that attorneys must verify the accuracy of information no matter where it comes from. Whether a lawyer gets help from an AI tool, a law student, or a fellow attorney, the lawyer signing the brief must attest to its accuracy, they said.
Justice C. Shannon Bacon was particularly withering in her criticism of Aarons. She told Aarons that there are “at least eight or nine provisions in the code of conduct that you violated.” Bacon said she was “really struggling with” Aarons’ claim to be unaware of AI hallucinations, noting that her 13-year-old nephew and 75-year-old stepmother are both aware of the problem.
“So counsel, do you watch the news? Do you listen to the radio? Do you read anything about what’s going on in the world? Because the problem with lawyers relying on AI hallucinations is an above-the-fold story every single day,” she said. “So either you buried your head in the sand—and that’s a choice to do that, an intentional choice to be uninformed—or you took a gamble, and neither of those are consistent with the code of conduct.”
Aarons responded that he submitted the brief a year ago and “a lot has come out in the last year.” However, the problem of lawyers using AI in briefs that cite made-up cases has been in the news regularly for well over three years.
Aarons added that the cases he cited in his brief were not fake, although his brief described them inaccurately. Bacon responded that there’s no “material distinction” between inaccurately describing a real case and citing a fake one, as the rules about candor to the court apply “with equal force” either way.
“I didn’t know that AI could hallucinate facts”
Aarons provided a statement when contacted by Ars today. He said:
In March 2025 I agreed to handle an appeal and used ChatGPT to summarize the trial proceedings. I wrote the brief but the table of contents and the summary contained numerous errors. At the time, I didn’t know that AI could hallucinate facts not only in my brief but in pleadings submitted by other attorneys. I am glad the court threw out my defective pleading and ordered the public defender to write a new brief on behalf of my former client. As for myself, I am remorseful but hopeful that the disciplinary board takes into account it was an honest mistake. It is a lesson learned for all professionals who rely upon this powerful but sometimes unstable technology.
Aarons told the court that he began by using Rev.com, a service that provides AI transcripts of audio files, and then put that transcript and other materials into ChatGPT.
“I believe I did confirm” that the trial transcript was accurate, he said when asked if he confirmed its accuracy before inputting it into ChatGPT. “The problem wasn’t in the transcript. It was when I loaded it and all the other information” into ChatGPT, he said. In addition to the transcript, Aarons said he put “the record proper, the statement of issues, and some of the discovery” into ChatGPT.
Aarons said he hoped the court would take steps to prevent other lawyers from making the same mistake he did, such as by issuing a standing order requiring that briefs contain a certificate of compliance regarding the use of AI. Justices treated Aaron’s suggestion as a distraction from the main problem, his failure to verify the accuracy of the brief.
“Assume with me that you had relied on the work of a first-year lawyer that was working for you and that they had just made stuff up… and you signed it. You’d be in the same exact soup you are right now,” Bacon said. “So the idea that, the suggestion in your briefing that because the court didn’t tell you at the time that you did this, ‘be careful,’ it somehow relieves you of obligation, falls on absolute deaf ears because the rules of professional conduct already tell you what your obligation is.”
“Your client is the one suffering”
“The other thing that’s completely missing from your response is anything about what this has done to your client,” Bacon went on to say. “That’s who I’m worried about. You have presented briefing to the court that we cannot rely on, and your client is the one suffering because of this far more than you will ever suffer.”
Chief Justice Julie Vargas similarly told Aarons, “I’m really interested with the approach you’re taking in this hearing. You seem to be telling us all the policy that we’ve been thinking about for years about what to do with AI, but you’re not talking about how to address the situation that’s in front of us, which has significant impacts on a criminal defendant who is in custody, who’s going to stay in custody until we resolve this matter. And I really don’t care about the policy concerns right now. I care about what we’re going to do with your client and what we should do in this circumstance based on the behavior that you showed us.”
Justice Michael Vigil said there’s nothing wrong with using AI to help write a legal argument as long as the lawyer verifies its accuracy. “It doesn’t matter what the tool is. It doesn’t matter how advanced the AI-generated program is or what improvements they make, whatever,” he said. “It doesn’t matter whether you use a C-student lawyer or a A-student lawyer [if] you didn’t check their work before you filed the brief. That’s the issue. And I wish, or I’m hoping you would focus on that, take responsibility for it.”
Aarons replied, “I hope I don’t present myself as not accepting responsibility. I mean, my only hope is that the mistakes that I made that somehow can prevent someone else down the line from repeating my mistake because the AI capacity is amazing.”
Lawyer didn’t tell client and family about ChatGPT use
Bacon criticized Aarons for not disclosing the problem to his client. “I have not. He’s a Spanish speaker and I wanted to see what happened today,” Aarons told Bacon when she asked if he told Sandoval about the problem.
Aarons said he was hired by Sandoval’s brother and cousin, and that he told them there was a problem with a brief. “They’re aware that there was a problem with the first brief that I filed and that the court’s looking at that. That’s pretty much it,” he said.
Bacon replied, “You didn’t say, ‘I relied on ChatGPT and it submitted lies to the court and the court is mad at me and now there’s a hearing.’ I’m guessing you didn’t tell your client’s family members that.”
“I didn’t talk about ChatGPT,” Aarons said. “I just said there was a problem with the brief that I filed.” Bacon told Aarons that his client needed to know the extent of the problem so he can make an informed decision “about whether you’re the right person to represent him.”
Bacon asked Aarons whether he was working on the case on a public defender contract or as private counsel. Aarons answered that he was hired as private counsel but hadn’t been paid yet.
“I’m not sure that’s going to happen,” Bacon replied.

'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'
- Published
A Nigerian man has shared the story of how he rose up out of "abject poverty" as a child, to become one of the leading UK academics in his field.
David Etor, 43, who grew up in Nigeria, only learned to read and write aged 12 and was told as a child that "nothing good will come out of you", but is now a lecturer in electrical and mechanical engineering at the University of Bristol.
He told the BBC how his family was so poor growing up that his mum would pretend to cook food in a kitchen they shared with others, "to protect our integrity" in front of neighbours.
"I didn't see a way out," he said.
'The poor called us poor'
Speaking to John Darvall on BBC Radio Bristol about the publication of his first book, Etor described growing up in a "compound" with several other families, all sharing a single kitchen, toilet and bathroom.
"It was a very poor neighbourhood. We were particularly very poor that the poor neighbours would refer to us as poor," he said.
"I do remember that there was a time where my mum would boil water.
"[She would] go back in and out, lift the lid, stir the water, go back into the room [and] come back as though she was preparing food...
"She would come back in with that pot of water after a couple of hours and it will be as though she's just finished cooking a meal, but it was just water.
"She was trying to protect our integrity."

To solve the problem, he designed and built a kind of "solar oven".
"It worked incredibly well," he said, which led to an award from the state government and a job.
He then completed an undergraduate degree at Newcastle University and a PhD at the University of Durham, before securing his current job in Bristol.
Sir Steve Webb, the former MP and Pensions Minister, who got to know Etor through the church in Bristol, called his achievements "remarkable".
"David's message is very much that people shouldn't be defined by their upbringing or their background," he said. "They shouldn't be written off."

BRICS leaders on Saturday (September 12, 2026) called for stronger cooperation in disease surveillance and medical product regulation, welcoming the establishment of a dedicated sub-working group to advance an integrated early warning system for the prevention and response to mass infectious diseases.
In their New Delhi Declaration, the leaders stressed the importance of strengthening health infrastructure and local production of medical products to enhance preparedness for future health emergencies and ensure timely, affordable and equitable access to healthcare services, vaccines, therapeutics and diagnostics.
They also called for strengthened collaboration among BRICS medical products regulatory authorities and welcomed efforts to develop a common GxP white paper consolidating regulatory best practices and technical approaches.
Public health emergencies transcend national borders
The leaders recognised that infectious disease outbreaks, zoonotic threats, antimicrobial resistance and other public health emergencies transcend national borders and require stronger international cooperation, timely information sharing and coordinated action.
"Acknowledging that infectious disease outbreaks, zoonotic threats, antimicrobial resistance and other public health emergencies transcend national borders and require strengthened international cooperation, timely information sharing and coordinated collective action, we underscore the importance of enhancing global health security through resilient surveillance systems, effective early warning mechanisms, and strengthened preparedness and response capacities," the declaration said.
The leaders recognising the central role of the World Health Organization and the amended International Health Regulations (2005), underscored the importance of resilient surveillance, early warning and rapid response systems and coordination.
"In this regard, we welcome the establishment of a dedicated Sub-Working Group to advance the BRICS Integrated Early Warning System for the prevention and response to Mass Infectious Diseases, and its Terms of Reference," they said.
Collective preparedness
The initiative is aimed at strengthening collective preparedness against infectious disease threats through closer coordination among member countries and faster sharing of information.
The declaration also called for greater regulatory cooperation to ensure that medical products remain available, accessible and meet standards of quality, safety and efficacy across BRICS countries.
"We encourage strengthened collaboration among BRICS Medical Products Regulatory Authorities by extending the scope of the existing Memorandum of Understanding on cooperation in the field of medical products regulation to the Regulatory Authorities of all BRICS member countries," the declaration said.
Collaborative regulatory approaches
They reiterated the importance of strengthening collaborative regulatory approaches to ensure the continued availability and accessibility of quality, safe and efficacious medical products.
The leaders also welcomed the collective efforts of BRICS regulatory authorities in developing the BRICS GxP White Paper.
"We welcome the collective efforts of BRICS Regulatory Authorities in developing the BRICS GxP White Paper, consolidating best practices of regulatory experience and technical approaches," the declaration said.
The GxP refers broadly to good-practice standards followed in areas such as manufacturing, laboratory and clinical processes, with the common framework expected to facilitate greater sharing of regulatory experience and technical approaches among member countries.
Strengthen domestic health infrastructure
The leaders also linked health security with stronger domestic health infrastructure and local production of medical products, calling for greater preparedness for future health emergencies.
"We emphasize the importance of strengthening health infrastructure and local production of medical products, enhancing preparedness for future health emergencies through stronger surveillance systems, laboratory networks, leveraging digital health technology and Artificial Intelligence," the declaration said.
They also called for technical cooperation among public health institutes, development of robust regulatory frameworks, skilled health workforces and collaborative research and development.
The declaration stressed that these measures were needed to improve access to healthcare products and services and strengthen the capacity of BRICS countries to respond collectively to health emergencies.
People-centred digital healthcare systems
The leaders also reaffirmed their commitment to people-centred digital healthcare systems and welcomed the BRICS Compendium on Digital Health Architecture for Continuum of Care, including access to healthcare in remote areas.
The leaders also supported the activities of the BRICS Vaccine Research and Development Centre and recognised the importance of collaboration in nuclear medicine.
They welcomed the activities of the BRICS Nuclear Medicine Working Group and noted the importance of the BRICS Health Journal in disseminating research findings and promoting scientific cooperation within the BRICS framework.
The declaration also emphasised the importance of sharing experiences, innovations and best practices among BRICS countries to improve health outcomes and advance universal health coverage.

New Delhi, Sep 14: In a significant crackdown on attempts to circumvent India’s prohibition on imports from Pakistan, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), has seized more than 362 metric tonnes of Pakistan-origin dry dates.
Acting on specific intelligence, DRI officers intercepted 13 containers of dry dates imported by a Mumbai-based firm at CFS Ambad, Nashik. The consignments had arrived from Jebel Ali, UAE, with import documents declaring the UAE as the country of origin.
Preliminary investigation revealed a carefully orchestrated transshipment arrangement designed to conceal the Pakistan-origin of the goods. The dry dates were initially shipped from Karachi Port, Pakistan, to Jebel Ali Port, UAE, in one set of containers aboard one vessel. At Jebel Ali, the goods were merely transshipped and transferred to another set of containers and loaded onto a different vessel for onward shipment to India through entities operated by Pakistani nationals.
Following the Pahalgam terror attack, the Government of India, in the interest of national security, imposed a complete prohibition on the direct or indirect import or transit of all goods originating in or exported from Pakistan, with effect from 2 May 2025, vide DGFT Notification No. 06/2025-26 dated 2 May 2025. In response, DRI, under “Operation Deep Manifest”, has been consistently identifying, intercepting and seizing Pakistan-origin goods attempted to be imported into India through third-country routing.
The seizure underscores DRI’s sustained resolve to identify, disrupt and dismantle sophisticated networks seeking to circumvent trade prohibitions through misdeclaration, transshipment and manipulation of documentation, thereby safeguarding national security and straightening supply chain integrity.

- A new trademark filing from South Korean publisher Neowiz may have revealed the title of the possible Lies of P sequel.
- “Wonders of O” appears in Neowiz’s trademark filing for the Lies of P sequel, hinting at a darker take on The Wizard of Oz.
- Previously, the Lies of P post-credits scene hinted at a Wizard of Oz connection by name-dropping the fairy tale’s main character, Dorothy.
About a year ago, South Korean game publisher Neowiz released a prequel DLC to Lies of P, titled Lies of P: Overture, and now they’re ready to return to the world of grim fairytale reinterpretations.
The publisher has trademarked “Wonders of O,” potentially revealing the title of a follow-up or sequel. Neowiz filed a new trademark with the European Union Intellectual Property Office on September 10, 2026, and the filing has now surfaced online on the official website.
The listing is for “virtual reality game software; interactive multimedia software for playing games,” similar to Neowiz’s Lies of P trademark. The similarities certainly make the connection to Lies of P more interesting, but they don’t necessarily confirm that Wonders of O is a direct sequel or follow-up.
However, the filing does suggest that Wonders of O could continue Lies of P’s approach of putting a dark spin on a classic fairy tale. While Lies of P reimagines Pinocchio, the title Wonders of O strongly points to The Wizard of Oz.
The most interesting part is that the post-credits scene of the 2023 soulslike game connects to The Wizard of Oz by revealing that the immortal alchemist Paracelsus is tracking down Dorothy as a new key subject for his organization.
For those unaware, Dorothy Gale serves as the main character of The Wizard of Oz. Along the Yellow Brick Road, she befriends the Cowardly Lion, the Tin Man, and the Scarecrow as they set out to find the Wizard in the popular fairy tale.
So, this listing and the Lies of P post-credits scene suggest the next game will be a darker retelling of The Wizard of Oz and will feature Dorothy as the main character, similar to how Lies of P had P, or Pinocchio.
Lies of P remains one of the best soulslike games, like Elden Ring, to play. With Round8 Studio and Neowiz returning for the sequel, Wonders of O is guaranteed to be another memorable soulslike experience.

Former prime minister Boris Johnson has hit out at Vladimir Putin after his train was involved in a near miss with a Russian drone close to the Ukraine-Poland border on Sunday.

A diplomatic train carrying Boris Johnson, Carl Bildt and security advisers from several European Union states had deliberately left the station at Yahodyn ahead of schedule and the foreign dignitaries were on their way back from the conference when a drone struck the line behind them.

Jaipur: Independents emerged as the decisive force in Rajasthan’s urban local body elections, limiting 
BJP
’s gains and keeping 
Congress
 competitive across several towns. BJP finished as the single largest party, but the scale of independent victories turned many civic bodies into arenas for post-poll negotiation rather than clear mandates.
According to final figures uploaded on the State Election Commission website, results had been declared in 10,235 of 10,244 wards by late Monday, with BJP winning 4,179, Congress 3,613 and independents picking up 2,273 to collectively take third position and establish themselves as potential kingmakers in urban local bodies where neither major party managed to cross the majority mark.
At the urban local body level, BJP secured majorities in four municipal corporations – Jaipur, Bhilwara, Kota and Udaipur – and emerged as the single largest party in Alwar. Of the 47 municipal councils, BJP won a clear majority in 11, Congress in six and independents or others in four. In Fatehpur, Congress was tied with an independent candidate.
The results give BJP the numerical edge, but not the sweep it sought in the first major statewide urban electoral test for the Bhajan Lal Sharma govt since it came to power in Dec 2023. Sharma campaigned extensively, holding roadshows in Ajmer, Bhilwara, Udaipur, Pali, Bikaner, Bharatpur, Jaipur, Alwar, Jodhpur and Kota. 
Even so, the party suffered reverses in key pockets and fell short in several prestige contests.
The sharpest setbacks came from politically symbolic terrain.
Jhalawar and Baran, former chief minister Vasundhara Raje’s strongholds for four decades, slipped out of BJP’s control. Congress won Jhalawar, while AAP made its political debut in the state by claiming control of its maiden municipal body in Baran.
Sharma also faced a difficult verdict in his home turf of Bharatpur despite his direct role in candidate selection. Independents won 36 wards there, compared with 20 for BJP and seven for Congress, leaving the ruling party far from a majority.
Pali delivered another blow. BJP lost the city to Congress despite its association with BJP state president Madan Rathore, cabinet minister Joraram Kumawat and former Union minister PP Choudhary.
The party also suffered setbacks in parts of Shekhawati and eastern Rajasthan. Its performance in Bikaner and Ajmer, where Congress ended BJP’s 36-year hold over the city, has sharpened concerns within the organisation, particularly with panchayat polls likely later this year.
Congress, though behind BJP in the overall tally, gained enough ground to make the point that BJP’s urban dominance remained incomplete. State Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra delivered a strong result for the party in his home turf of Sikar and Laxmangarh, strengthening his position within the state unit.
In Tonk, Congress managed an edge in Sachin Pilot’s political turf even though the former deputy chief minister largely stayed away from campaigning and ticket distribution. The party also mounted a serious challenge in Jodhpur, former chief minister Ashok Gehlot’s political base, where Union minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat campaigned extensively over the past month.
The CPM also entered the winners’ list by commanding enough numbers to form the board in Nokha, Bikaner.
The strongest signal from the verdict is the independent vote. With 2,273 wards, independents are set to influence control in several bodies where neither BJP nor Congress has a clear majority. Their performance points to the continuing strength of local networks, candidate reputation and ward-level grievances over party loyalty in many towns.
The State Election Commission Monday postponed, until further orders, elections for chairperson and deputy chairperson in four urban local bodies after technical glitches in EVMs delayed the declaration of results. The affected bodies include Jaipur, Jodhpur and Kota municipal corporations, and Suket municipality in Kota. During counting, results from some booths could not be released due to EVM malfunctions, leaving the results in these bodies incomplete. The Commission said fresh dates would be announced later.
The SEC has ordered repolling at 10 polling stations in Jaipur, Jodhpur, Kota and Suket. Repolling will be held on Sept 16 from 7am to 6pm, with counting on Sept 17 from 8am at designated centres.
The affected booths include five in Jaipur Municipal Corporation, one in Jodhpur Municipal Corporation, three in Kota Municipal Corporation and one in Suket municipality. The Commission said the number of votes affected by the malfunction exceeded the victory margins between the nearest rival candidates, requiring repolling.
In Jaipur, BJP crossed the majority mark with 78 seats in the 150-member Jaipur Municipal Corporation. Results of four wards were withheld after EVMs developed technical snags, leaving counting incomplete.
Elections were held in two phases, on Sept 9 and 11, across 309 urban local bodies — 10 municipal corporations, 47 municipal councils and 252 municipalities. The increase in the number of bodies since the previous elections followed the creation of new municipalities, expansion and reorganisation of existing urban areas, and delimitation.
The results mark a shift from the map that emerged after the previous municipal elections, held between Nov 2019 and Feb 2021, when Rajasthan had 196 urban local bodies with 7,500 wards. After the election of mayors and chairpersons, Congress controlled 123 bodies, BJP 64, and Independents and other parties nine.

Tamil Nadu Minister for Health and Family Welfare K.G. Arunraj on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) announced in the Legislative Assembly that the State government would implement a Statewide mission to reduce the amount of salt in the daily diet of the public.
Dr. Arunraj said non-communicable diseases such as hypertension, cardiovascular diseases, stroke, and kidney disorders were among the most important public health challenges in Tamil Nadu. Nearly 50% of medically certified deaths in Tamil Nadu are caused by cardiovascular diseases. Approximately 1.8 crore people in Tamil Nadu are living with hypertension.
The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends that a person should consume less than five grams of salt a day. However, scientific studies indicate that the people of Tamil Nadu consume an average of 7 to 8 grams of salt per day. Studies have also found that approximately 88% of the salt consumed as part of the South Indian diet comes from salt added during cooking at home. Global scientific studies have established that even a reduction of just one gram of salt per day can significantly lower blood pressure, he said.
Further, an international study involving approximately 21,000 people who used a low-sodium salt substitute, in which a portion of the sodium was replaced with potassium, demonstrated a 14% reduction in strokes and a 12% reduction in overall mortality. Based on this scientific evidence, the State government has decided to formulate and implement an integrated strategy to reduce high salt consumption in Tamil Nadu, Dr. Arunraj said.
Statewide survey
Announcing the key initiatives under the mission, Dr. Arunraj said for the first time, a Statewide survey based on urine samples would be undertaken to scientifically determine the current level of salt consumption among the people of Tamil Nadu.
Standards would be implemented to gradually reduce the amount of salt used in kitchens under the direct control of the government, including those serving the Nutritious Meal Programme, the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme, government hospitals and hostels, he said.
The feasibility of making available to the public a low-sodium salt substitute, in which a portion of sodium is replaced with potassium and which does not produce a noticeable difference in taste, would be studied as a pilot project in selected areas, he said.
Through the ‘Makkalai Thedi Maruthuvam’ initiative and Health and Wellness Centres, people with hypertension would receive systematic counselling on reducing salt intake. A Statewide awareness campaign will be undertaken to educate people about salt content in food and simple ways to gradually reduce the excessive use of salt in everyday home cooking, he added.
